toolGroups.group: General AI assistants and research tools
toolGroups.category_overview: These six are horizontal assistants rather than departmental systems. Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT Enterprise compete as general chat-plus-agent platforms, while NotebookLM (now Gemini Notebook) and Perplexity specialise in grounded research: the former over uploaded documents, the latter over the live web with citations. Overlap is growing: the big assistants offer deep research, file creation, connectors and agents; Perplexity offers third-party models (GPT, Gemini, Claude) inside its own interface. Enterprises usually standardise on the assistant bundled with their productivity suite, add one frontier chat platform for knowledge workers, and buy Perplexity Enterprise or Gemini Notebook as a niche research tool. Key procurement differences: training defaults (enterprise tiers exclude training by default; consumer tiers of Gemini, Claude and Perplexity differ), compliance coverage (varies by tier and sub-feature) and pricing model (flat seats versus seat-plus-usage). The claim that Gemini Enterprise routes work to Claude is not verified on an opened page.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.vendor: Google (Alphabet). Family: Gemini app (Google AI Plus/Pro/Ultra), Gemini in Google Workspace, Gemini Enterprise (Google Cloud; Business/Standard/Plus editions).
tools.what_it_is: Google's general AI assistant. Surfaces: the Gemini web/mobile app; the side panel in Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Chat, Drive and Vids; Chrome; and the Gemini Enterprise app on Google Cloud with connectors to non-Google systems.
key_capabilities: Deep Research, Canvas, Gems, Gemini Live, image/video generation
Drafting and summarisation in Gmail/Docs; Meet note-taking
Gemini Enterprise: permission-aware search over connectors and no-code agents (connector count and multi-model routing not verified)
Bundled Gemini Notebook (ex-NotebookLM) for source-grounded research
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Workspace: content is not human-reviewed or used for model training outside your domain without permission; Gemini app conversation auto-delete options 3, 18 or 36 months, default 18 months. Gemini in Workspace apps and the Gemini app have FedRAMP High; SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701/42001 and HIPAA support per Google's privacy hub. Google states Gemini Notebook and Gemini in Chrome do NOT support ISO/SOC/FedRAMP and are not covered by the HIPAA BAA. Gemini Enterprise Standard/Plus (and Notebook Enterprise) support data residency, CMEK (US/EU multi-region), VPC-SC and Access Transparency, with some limits (e.g. not with Grounding with Google Search); the Business edition's controls are not verified. Consumer plans sit under consumer terms.
tools.licensing_pricing: Consumer (verified on gemini.google/subscriptions): AI Plus $4.99, AI Pro $19.99, AI Ultra from $99.99 to $199.99/month. Workspace Business Standard US$14/user/month (annual) including Gemini: NOT verified (pricing page text showed no prices); Workspace page confirms Gemini Notebook is included in plans and Enterprise is contact-sales. Gemini Enterprise per-seat prices (Business ~$21, Standard/Plus ~$30) and pay-as-you-go overages: not verified on an opened page; treat as indicative only.
tools.integrations: Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Chat, Drive, Vids, Chrome. Specific third-party connector list (Microsoft 365, Slack, Salesforce, etc.) and the Workspace MCP server: not verified.
tools.recent_developments: 16 Jul 2026: NotebookLM renamed Gemini Notebook (verified). Gemini 4 Argon is available to AI Pro/Ultra (verified on subscriptions page). Other items (Cloud Next Apr 2026 announcements, Aug 2026 pay-as-you-go edition, 8 Oct 2026 Gemini agent): not re-verified here.
tools.best_fit_departments: Strongest where Workspace is the system of record: Core 01, 04, 11, 13, 18, 28, 29, 31, 33, 39, 54 and analytics-heavy 16, 20, 50 via Sheets. Specialist fits (06-08, 23, 47-49, 51, 53) are weak: a general assistant without domain tooling.
tools.training_notes: Master @-mentioning Drive files, Gems, Deep Research and citation checking, and understand how sharing permissions and DLP bound what Gemini can see; admins must choose edition and set retention. Core 6-8 h; Advanced 12-16 h; Specialist 20-30 h.
tools.caveats: Overlapping products under one brand with different terms; features vary by edition and region; Notebook/Chrome compliance gap; personal Google accounts fall under consumer terms; enterprise prices unverified; outputs need verification.

toolGroups.category_overview: All six tools are Microsoft products that share one identity, permission and compliance plane (Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, Purview), but they sit on two different licensing stacks. Microsoft 365 Copilot (now marketed as "Microsoft Copilot") is a per-user add-on, and Copilot in Word, Excel and Teams are not separate products but surfaces of that single licence; the free Copilot Chat tier gives enterprise-data-protected chat without the in-app features. Power BI Copilot and Power Automate belong to the Fabric/Power Platform stack, which is priced by capacity (Fabric CU) or by maker/bot licence plus consumption-based Copilot Credits, so the "Copilot" label hides very different cost models. Overlap is real: Teams recap competes with Teams Premium, Excel Copilot and Power BI Copilot both answer data questions, and Power Automate cloud flows compete with Copilot Studio agent flows. Enterprises already on Microsoft 365 E3/E5 usually standardise on the Copilot add-on (or the new E7 bundle) for knowledge workers, Power BI on Fabric capacity for analytics, and Power Automate Premium plus a governed Centre of Excellence for automation, while using Purview and DLP as the common control layer.

tools.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Microsoft Copilot family; product renamed from "Microsoft 365 Copilot" to "Microsoft Copilot" in August 2026, licences may still carry the old name)
tools.what_it_is: An AI assistant embedded in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, Loop and OneNote, plus the standalone Microsoft Copilot app (copilot.cloud.microsoft) with Chat, Search, Notebooks, Pages and agents. It grounds large language models in the user's Microsoft Graph content (mail, files, chats, meetings) while honouring existing permissions.
key_capabilities: Graph-grounded chat with optional web grounding and citations
Researcher and Analyst reasoning agents producing reports, decks and data analyses
Copilot Notebooks and Pages for persistent, shareable working context
Edit with Copilot (Agent Mode) that makes multi-step changes inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Copilot Cowork task delegation and federated Copilot connectors over MCP (not verified against an opened page)
Agent Builder and declarative agents governed from the Microsoft 365 admin center
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Paid licence and no-cost Copilot Chat (Enterprise Data Protection): prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models; data is covered by the DPA. Copilot surfaces only content the user can already view; admins get Purview retention, audit and eDiscovery over Copilot interactions. The EU Data Boundary does not apply to web search queries, and Anthropic-provided models are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments. Stated commitments include GDPR, ISO/IEC 27018, DPA and BAA; Microsoft Copilot is listed in the Office 365 FedRAMP scope pages. Other certifications (ISO 42001, SOC 2 Type 2) and the Multi-Geo/ADR date: not verified. Admins choose whether OpenAI or Anthropic subprocessor models are used.
tools.licensing_pricing: Add-on priced at USD 30 per user per month on annual commitment (USD 360/year) per an independent 2026 guide (EPC Group); Microsoft's own pricing page could not be retrieved. Included in Microsoft 365 E7 (USD 99 per user per month, launching 1 May 2026, per Directions on Microsoft; E7 bundles E5, Copilot, Agent 365 and Entra Suite per EPC). Copilot Business is an add-on for tenants up to 300 users with annual commitment (Learn; USD 21 per independent source). Prerequisite plans include M365 E3/E5/F1/F3, Business Basic/Standard/Premium, Office 365 E1/E3/E5 and others; GCC, GCC High and DoD add-ons exist (Learn). Copilot Chat is no-cost with eligible M365 subscriptions; usage-based billing details not verified.
tools.integrations: Microsoft Graph (Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams), Copilot connectors, Power Platform connectors (separately licensed), Dataverse/Dynamics search, Purview, Planner agent, Copilot Analytics in Viva Insights.
tools.recent_developments: Aug 2026: app renamed Microsoft Copilot with new URL copilot.cloud.microsoft (rollout from mid-August, MC1454108, per futurework.blog); Learn docs state "Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot". 1 May 2026: Microsoft 365 E7 launch with Copilot included. Agent Mode GA in Word/Excel/PowerPoint in April 2026 (exact date not verified). Later 2026 items (Cowork, Vision, model additions, Pages storage) not verified.
tools.best_fit_departments: Strong for Office of the CEO, Board Secretariat, HR Business Partnering, PMO, Sales, Legal drafting, Learning & Development and any role living in Outlook/Teams/Word. Weak fit where the listed task is structured-data or system-specific: Accounts Payable invoice extraction (Power Automate/AI Builder), Supply Chain demand insights and Enterprise Applications & ERP (Power BI/ERP tools), and specialist Regulatory Compliance control evidence.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master grounding prompts with files and people, verifying citations, sensitivity labels and oversharing hygiene, when to use Researcher/Analyst versus chat, reviewing Agent Mode edits, and Notebooks. Core 6-10 hours for general users; Advanced 12-20 hours for agents, Notebooks and Analyst; Specialist 20-40 hours for Agent Builder, connectors and governance.
tools.caveats: Outputs are not guaranteed factual and must be reviewed. Permission hygiene is a prerequisite because Copilot exposes anything a user can already open. Government clouds lack Edit with Copilot (Learn service description). EU Data Boundary excludes Anthropic models and web queries. Annual commitment plus emerging usage-based billing complicates budgeting, and the 2026 rename causes documentation confusion. Price rests on independent sources.

tools.name: Power BI Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Copilot in Power BI, part of Copilot in Microsoft Fabric)
tools.what_it_is: Generative AI built into Power BI Desktop, the Power BI service, Power BI apps and mobile. Business users chat with reports and semantic models in a report pane or a full-screen standalone Copilot; authors use it to create report pages, narrative visuals and DAX queries. It runs on Fabric capacity rather than a per-user licence.
key_capabilities: Summarise an open report or answer data questions in the report Copilot pane (GA)
Standalone cross-item Copilot that finds and queries any report or model the user can access (preview)
App-scoped Copilot with author-verified answers (preview)
Generate report pages, narrative visuals and summaries in email subscriptions
Write and explain DAX queries; create measure descriptions; Copilot in web modeling
Power BI data answers inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (not verified)
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Processed by Azure OpenAI Service hosted by Microsoft; data stays within the organisation's tenant boundary and is not used to train foundation models; Copilot does not store prompts or responses after the session ends (Learn). Copilot reads only data the user can access. Tenant admins can enable or disable Copilot; sovereign clouds are not supported. Cross-geo processing default settings, RLS/OLS enforcement detail, customer-managed keys, and SOC 2/ISO 27001/FedRAMP scope for Power BI: not verified.
tools.licensing_pricing: No per-user Copilot SKU: requires paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher or Power BI Premium P1+; trial and free SKUs are not supported (Learn). Usage is metered in capacity units: 100 CU-seconds per 1,000 input tokens (10 cached); output rate not re-verified. Microsoft pricing page: Power BI Pro USD 14 and Premium Per User USD 24 per user per month (paid yearly); Pro is included in Microsoft 365 E5 and Office 365 E5. Independent (Colrows): F2 about USD 262.80/month PAYG, F64 about USD 8,409.60 PAYG. A Fabric Copilot capacity can bill Copilot usage centrally (Learn).
tools.integrations: Microsoft Fabric (OneLake, Data Factory, data agents), Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Excel export, Teams, Purview, Dynamics/Dataverse and SQL sources via Power BI connectors; relevant to FP&A, People Analytics, RevOps, PMO and Supply Chain reporting.
tools.recent_developments: Standalone and app-scoped Copilot are in preview (Learn). Fabric Copilot capacity feature documented. Specific 2025-2026 dated items (Apr 2025 F2 opening, Sept 2026 GA items, Q&A visual retirement) not verified.
tools.best_fit_departments: Best for Business Intelligence & Analytics, FP&A, People Analytics, Sales/Revenue Operations, Supply Chain, Service Delivery, PMO and executive consumers. Weaker for Market Research & Competitive Intelligence (external data rarely modelled), Corporate Strategy scenario analysis (not a what-if engine), Internal Audit control testing, and Compensation/DEI where sensitive data demands strict RLS before enabling.
tools.training_notes: Model owners must prepare data for AI and mark models approved; authors need DAX review skills and prompt specificity using real field names; consumers need to read warnings and verify numbers; admins must monitor CU consumption and regional settings. Core 6-10 hours for consumers; Advanced 12-20 hours for report authors; Specialist 20-40 hours for model owners and capacity admins.
tools.caveats: Capacity cost and throttling are the main risk: an F2 can be exhausted by light use (Colrows field claim), and consumption rates can change. Standalone Copilot is preview; sovereign clouds unsupported; English works best. Outputs can be inaccurate without curated models. Some third-party guides still state an F64 minimum, which is outdated per Learn.

tools.what_it_is: The Copilot pane and "Edit with Copilot" mode inside Excel on Windows, Mac, web and mobile. It analyses workbook data, writes and explains formulas, builds PivotTables and charts, applies formatting and, in editing mode, changes the workbook directly, including running Python. A separate Excel Agent in Copilot Chat creates new workbooks from a description.
key_capabilities: Generate, apply and explain formulas across multiple sheets
Surface insights as charts, PivotTables, trends and outliers
Edit with Copilot (Agent Mode): add or rename sheets, modify ranges, build tables and visuals in place
Plan mode that outlines steps before changing anything (not verified)
Python in Edit with Copilot for analysis, automation and data transformation (Windows, Mac, web; release notes 25 Aug 2026)
Web grounding with citations and pulling data from other OneDrive/SharePoint workbooks (not verified)
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Inherits Microsoft Copilot enterprise data protection: prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models. Interactions are governable via Purview. Government clouds: Edit with Copilot is not yet available in GCC, GCC High or DoD, which limits structured-data analysis there (Learn service description). Connected-experiences dependency and Excel Agent stage/language limits: not verified.
tools.licensing_pricing: No standalone SKU. Requires the Microsoft Copilot add-on (independent guide: USD 30 per user per month, annual commitment) on an eligible Microsoft 365 plan, or Microsoft 365 E7 which includes Copilot. Consumer-plan credit limits: not verified. Copilot Business covers tenants up to 300 users (Learn).
tools.integrations: OneDrive/SharePoint, Python in Excel, Power BI export, Copilot Chat Excel Agent, Word and PowerPoint for downstream reporting, Purview labels.
tools.recent_developments: Agent Mode GA in April 2026 (exact date not verified). 25 Aug 2026: Python support in Edit with Copilot (Windows, Mac, web) per release notes. The preview =COPILOT() function has been retired: cached values remain but recalculation returns #NAME? (Microsoft Support); retirement date not verified.
tools.best_fit_departments: FP&A (variance narratives, quick scenario tables), Accounting & Financial Reporting (reconciliation support, explaining inherited formulas) and Treasury (cash-flow scenario drafts) fit well as drafting and exploration aids. Taxation is a weaker fit: document extraction and tax research are better served by specialist tools, and Copilot output should not be relied on for finance or legal decisions without review.
tools.training_notes: Learners must format data as tables with clear headers, keep files in OneDrive/SharePoint, understand Chat-only versus editing modes, verify every formula and Python output, use version history, and know the retired COPILOT() function. Advanced 12-20 hours for finance teams; Core 6-10 hours for occasional users.
tools.caveats: Outputs are non-deterministic; the independent test claim (inconsistent depreciation and WACC) is not verified. Workbooks that used =COPILOT() now break. Editing features are missing in government clouds. Large or messy ranges reduce reliability.

It lives in the Power Automate web portal and Teams app, the Power Automate for desktop application, and increasingly as agent flows inside Copilot Studio.

tools.enterprise_data_handling: Copilot runs on Azure OpenAI within Azure; prompts and outputs are not used to train Microsoft or third-party models unless the tenant admin opts in; no storage or eyes-on review of inputs/outputs for abuse monitoring (Learn FAQ). Generally available Copilot features are on by default, and cross-region data movement may need admin allowance (Learn). Dataverse encryption, Purview 90-day audit retention, FedRAMP High/DISA levels, SOC 2/ISO scope and GCC availability: not verified.
tools.licensing_pricing: Per Microsoft pricing page (paid yearly): Premium USD 15 per user per month; Process USD 150 per bot per month; Hosted Process USD 215 per bot per month; Process Mining add-on USD 5,000 per tenant per month (Premium only). Process licence entitles cloud flows to 250,000 actions per day (Learn). Pay-as-you-go USD 0.60 per premium cloud flow run per independent FlowForma. Agent flows bill 13 Copilot Credits per 100 actions per independent BabyBots (free exemption for M365 Copilot users via agent trigger per same source). Seeded AI Builder credits and add-ons reach end of life 1 November 2026, replaced by Copilot Credits (Learn). Per-user daily action limits (40k/6k) not verified.

tools.best_fit_departments: Business Operations & Process Excellence is the strongest fit (process mining plus automation). Accounts Payable & Receivable fits for invoice extraction and exception routing but now carries Copilot Credit costs. Workplace Administration & Facilities fits for request routing and notifications, though organisations with ServiceNow may route tickets there instead.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master triggers, actions and connectors, error handling and retries, solution-aware flows, environment and DLP strategy, licensing and request limits, RPA basics, AI Builder credit consumption, and reviewing Copilot-generated flows before saving. Core 6-10 hours for approvers and consumers; Advanced 12-20 hours for makers; Specialist 20-40 hours for RPA, process mining and Centre of Excellence roles.
tools.caveats: Licensing is complex: premium connectors, request limits and the AI Builder-to-Copilot-Credits shift can raise costs (the 2-4x figure is unverified). Third-party connectors move data outside Microsoft's compliance boundary. Agent flows consume Copilot Credit capacity. Several compliance and government-cloud claims were removed as unverified.

toolGroups.category_overview: These six tools form the output layer on top of general assistants and office suites: they turn text, data and documents into decks, graphics, prototypes and document summaries. Gamma and Canva compete for prompt-to-presentation and on-brand collateral (Gamma launched Gamma Imagine in March 2026 to take on Canva and Adobe, per TechCrunch). Adobe Firefly is the image/video engine marketed on commercial safety and Content Credentials. Acrobat AI Assistant is a different category (document comprehension over PDFs). Figma AI and FigJam AI are the product-design pair sharing one seat model and one AI-credit pool. Enterprises typically standardise on the suite they already license and allow one AI presentation tool under a Business/Enterprise tier where content training is contractually off. Recurring governance issues are consumption-based AI credits and default content training on lower tiers (verified for Figma and Gamma Pro; Canva and Adobe claims could not be re-opened and are marked not verified).

toolGroups.category_overview: These six tools span IDE assistants (GitHub Copilot, Gemini Code Assist, Amazon Q Developer), an AI-native editor (Cursor), a terminal/cloud coding agent (Claude Code) and the open-source test framework (Playwright) that all of them now drive through MCP servers and agent definitions. They compete head-on in agentic multi-file coding, automated PR review and enterprise controls, and increasingly resell the same frontier models: Copilot and Cursor offer Claude, GPT and Gemini, while Claude Code itself runs inside VS Code and Cursor and on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry. 2026 was a consolidation year: Google stopped selling new Code Assist subscriptions (Oct 9) in favour of Antigravity, AWS announced Q Developer's end of support for Kiro (Apr 30 2027), SpaceX folded Cursor into a Grok/X bundle (Oct 12), and GitHub moved to usage-metered AI Credits (June 1). Enterprises typically standardise on GitHub Copilot where GitHub is already the SCM, add Claude Code or Cursor for agentic work, keep the hyperscaler assistant matching their primary cloud, and adopt Playwright with its MCP server as the neutral QA layer. Procurement now has to track usage-based metering and model-provider retention terms as closely as seat prices.

toolGroups.category_overview: These six platforms embed AI inside the system of record each vendor already owns: ServiceNow for IT, employee and customer service plus GRC, Salesforce for CRM, SAP for ERP/procurement/supply chain, Workday for HCM and finance, Atlassian for work management, and UiPath for automation that crosses systems. They overlap increasingly at the edges: ServiceNow, Workday, Salesforce and SAP all now sell employee self-service agents and cross-vendor agent governance (AI Control Tower, Agent System of Record, Agentforce 360, SAP AI Agent Hub), and ServiceNow, Workday, UiPath and Atlassian expose MCP-based action layers so third-party assistants such as Claude or Copilot can act inside them. Enterprises typically standardise on the AI of whichever platform holds the data (ServiceNow for ITSM, Salesforce for CRM, SAP for ERP, Workday for HR, Jira for engineering/PMO) and use UiPath where work spans systems, rather than buying a separate assistant per platform. The common 2025-2026 shift is from per-seat add-ons to consumption metering (assists, Flex Credits, AI Units, Rovo credits, Platform Units), so budget governance, output review and admin controls are the shared training themes. ISO/IEC 42001 certification was confirmed for ServiceNow, Salesforce, SAP, Workday and UiPath; it was not verified for Atlassian.

toolGroups.category_overview: The six tools form three layers. Gong is conversation and revenue intelligence that sits on top of the CRM; HubSpot's Breeze Assistant and Agent Hub are AI native to the CRM itself; LinkedIn's Sales Navigator and Hiring Assistant monetise LinkedIn's member graph for prospecting and recruiting; Google Ads AI (AI Max, Performance Max, Ask Advisor) and Meta Advantage+ are opaque optimisation suites inside the two dominant ad platforms. Gong, HubSpot and Sales Navigator overlap on account research and outreach drafting and are increasingly wired together (Gong exposes MCP servers to HubSpot and Microsoft 365 Copilot; Sales Navigator Advanced Plus syncs into HubSpot, Salesforce, Dynamics and Oracle). Google and Meta compete for the same performance budgets and are converging on "give us a URL and a budget" automation while removing manual controls. Enterprises usually standardise on one CRM-native assistant, add Gong for enterprise sales coaching and forecasting, licence LinkedIn seats to sales and talent teams, and treat Google and Meta AI as unavoidable defaults that marketers must learn to steer rather than tools they choose.

tools.vendor: Gong.io Inc. Gong markets the platform as the "Gong Revenue AI OS" with modules Gong Engage, Gong Forecast, Gong Enable, Gong Agents and Gong Assistant.
tools.what_it_is: Gong records and transcribes sales calls, meetings and emails, then uses AI to summarise conversations, flag deal risk, coach reps and forecast revenue. It lives in its own web and mobile app and is surfaced inside Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Teams and Zoom; since February 2026 it also exposes MCP servers so Microsoft 365 Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce and HubSpot agents can query Gong data.

tools.enterprise_data_handling: Single enterprise contract (no self-serve tier). Gong's trust page states "Your data is never used to train generative AI models" and that customer data is not co-mingled; encryption, MFA and least-privilege access are listed. Default retention is up to three years or the contract duration, whichever is shorter, with custom retention on request and permanent deletion 30 days after termination. The trust page lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, 27017, 27018, 27701, ISO 42001, PCI DSS SAQ-D, CSA STAR and EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. HIPAA-related security requirements are listed, but covered-entity status and FedRAMP are not verified. Gong help docs say an admin can choose an EU data centre, whereas a Dec 2025 third-party (competitor Oliv) DPA review claimed US-only storage, so confirm residency contractually. Redaction, deny lists, consent management and SSO details were not re-verified.
tools.licensing_pricing: No published list prices. The pricing page confirms per-user licences plus a platform fee based on users supported, with quotes from a sales form by team size. Third-party estimate (Docket, May 2026): roughly US$1,400-3,000 per user per year depending on bundle, platform fee US$5,000-50,000, implementation US$15,000-65,000. Contract-term length (2-3 years) is not verified. Not bundled with any suite.

Core 6-8 hours for sellers; Advanced 12-16 hours for RevOps admins (editorial estimates).

toolGroups.category_overview: All four tools sit on the post-sale side of the customer lifecycle but on different layers. Zendesk AI and Fin compete head-on for autonomous ticket resolution and agent-assist in the contact centre: both now bill per outcome or resolution as well as (Zendesk) per seat, and both can run on rival help desks (Forethought AI Agents by Zendesk on Salesforce or Freshworks; Fin on Zendesk, Salesforce, HubSpot or Freshdesk). Gainsight works upstream in customer success, mining emails, meetings and tickets for renewal risk and expansion signals, while Qualtrics spans the whole journey, measuring experience and increasingly acting on it through Experience Agents. The 2026 consolidation wave reshapes vendor choice: Salesforce closed its acquisition of Fin on 10 September 2026, Zendesk completed its Forethought purchase in March 2026, and Qualtrics' $6.75B Press Ganey Forsta acquisition (May 2026) was confirmed in Qualtrics' own release. CRM and help-desk allegiance now determines which AI is practical to standardise on. Enterprises typically standardise on one help-desk AI (Zendesk or Fin/Intercom), Gainsight or CRM-native tooling for success, and Qualtrics for voice-of-customer, then connect signals through CRM integrations or MCP. (The ~$3.6B Fin price was not re-verified from an opened page.)

toolGroups.category_overview: These three tools are vertical specialists anchored to a proprietary corpus or system of record rather than general assistants: CoCounsel sells agentic AI on top of Thomson Reuters' Westlaw, Practical Law and Checkpoint content; Datasite embeds AI inside the virtual data room where deal documents already sit; Optro (formerly AuditBoard) embeds agents inside the GRC system of record. They barely overlap with one another, but all three compete for budget and attention with horizontal assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft 365 Copilot, and each has shipped or announced MCP connectors in 2026 so corporate instances of those assistants can reach their governed content and workflows under existing permissions. Enterprises typically standardise on one platform per function (legal research/drafting, deal rooms, GRC) and pair it with a horizontal assistant, because switching costs are driven by the underlying content subscriptions, deal archives or control libraries rather than the AI layer. Pricing is contract-based with no transparent enterprise list price except CoCounsel's self-serve small-firm tiers. The shared governance pattern is explicit no-training commitments, security attestations (details differ per vendor and some are verified only on vendor pages noted per tool), and citation traceability with human approval as the primary control.

toolGroups.group: Security, cloud operations and observability AI
toolGroups.category_overview: These seven tools are embedded, platform-native assistants and agents rather than general chat tools, and each is only as good as the telemetry it sits on. Microsoft Security Copilot, CrowdStrike Charlotte AI and Google Gemini in Security compete directly as SOC triage and investigation agents (departments 45/47). Microsoft Purview is the data-governance counterpart (department 48), and it also governs Copilot and other AI use. Azure Copilot, Datadog Bits AI and Dynatrace Intelligence (formerly Davis AI) address cloud and SRE operations (departments 43/44), with Datadog and Dynatrace competing as observability platforms. Enterprises usually standardise on the AI of the platform they already run, such as Microsoft 365 E5 and Azure, Falcon, Google SecOps, Datadog or Dynatrace, rather than buying across vendors. In all seven the pricing model is consumption or bundle based (SCUs, credits, commitments, ingestion), and the dominant 2025-26 trend is a move from chat assistants to semi-autonomous agents that need human-approval guardrails.

tools.name: Microsoft Security Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Microsoft Security product family: Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, Sentinel)
tools.what_it_is: A generative-AI security assistant and agent platform. It works in a standalone portal and embedded inside Defender, Entra, Intune and Purview. It summarises incidents, guides investigations and runs autonomous agents such as Phishing Triage and Conditional Access Optimization.
key_capabilities: Incident and alert summarisation with step-by-step response guidance
Embedded agents in Defender, Entra, Intune and Purview (phishing triage, vulnerability remediation, alert triage)
Promptbooks and a standalone natural-language investigation workspace
Partner-built and community-built (no-code) agents
Cross-product context spanning identities, devices, data, clouds and apps
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Applies to the commercial service. Customer Data is stored in the Workspace geo chosen at onboarding, which cannot be changed afterwards. Docs state data is not shared with OpenAI or used to train the Azure OpenAI foundation model. A separate data-sharing setting is ON by default for customers without an M365 E5/E7 licence (E5/E7 customers have different defaults per the Learn page). If opted in, prompts and responses go to Microsoft for product improvement and may be stored outside the chosen geo, and uploaded-file content may be human-reviewed. Admins (Global Admin, Security Admin with Capacity Contributor) can change it. Customer Data is deleted within 180 days of removing all provisioned capacity, and session data after 180 days of inactivity. Agent emails or Teams messages can cross geographic boundaries in transit. SOC 2, ISO 27001 and HIPAA attestations were not verified on opened pages.
tools.licensing_pricing: Standalone: provisioned capacity in Security Compute Units (SCUs). The worked example on the pricing page uses USD 4 per provisioned SCU per hour (billed monthly) and USD 6 per overage SCU, minimum 1 SCU. Included at no added cost for eligible Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers: 400 SCUs per month per 1,000 paid user licences, capped at 10,000 SCUs per month, on a phased rollout that began 18 Nov 2025.
tools.integrations: Microsoft Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview and Sentinel; partner-built agents. ServiceNow-style ticketing integration was not verified. Relevant to departments 45, 47 and 48 through embedded Purview and Entra agents.
tools.recent_developments: Nov 2025 (Ignite): Security Copilot bundled into Microsoft 365 E5, later extended to E7. About a dozen new agents embedded in Defender, Entra, Intune and Purview. Microsoft markets the product around agents rather than the earlier chat-assistant framing.
tools.best_fit_departments: 47 Cybersecurity Operations (best fit: triage, hunting, incident summaries). 48 Security Governance, Risk & Privacy fits via the Purview and Entra agents. 45 IT Infrastructure is a weaker fit, limited to Intune and Entra device and identity tasks.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master prompt scoping, reading agent evidence and verdicts, SCU consumption monitoring, role and permission setup, and the data-sharing setting. Suggested 24-32 hours (Specialist band), including supervised alert-triage labs.
tools.caveats: Value depends on the Microsoft security stack being deployed. SCU consumption is hard to forecast. The E5 inclusion is phased, so some tenants may not yet have it. The data-sharing default is ON for non-E5/E7 customers and should be reviewed by privacy teams. Outputs can be wrong and need analyst validation.

toolGroups.group: Data, analytics and AI development platforms
toolGroups.category_overview: These seven tools sit at different layers of the data and AI stack. Databricks Genie Code and Snowflake CoCo/Cortex are AI assistants and AI functions embedded in the two leading data platforms, serving data engineering and analytics inside their own governance models. Tableau Pulse is a business-user metrics and insights layer, and competes with Power BI Copilot elsewhere in the handbook. Google AI Studio, Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) and Amazon Bedrock are hyperscaler model and agent platforms for building RAG and agent applications, and each competes for the same workloads. MLflow is the vendor-neutral open-source layer for tracing, evaluation and registries that can sit across the others, and is also bundled into Databricks. Enterprises usually standardise on the data platform they already run (Databricks or Snowflake) and the cloud AI platform that matches their hyperscaler contract. They use Google AI Studio only for prototyping, and move production work to the governed cloud tier.

tools.name: Databricks Assistant
tools.vendor: Databricks. Now marketed as Genie Code, part of the Databricks Genie family. The brief's name is out of date.
tools.what_it_is: Databricks Assistant was renamed Genie Code in March 2026 and became an autonomous agent for data teams. It runs inside the Databricks workspace (notebooks, SQL editor, Lakeflow Pipelines Editor, AI/BI dashboards, MLflow). It plans multi-step tasks, writes and runs code, and fixes errors, within the user's Unity Catalog permissions.
key_capabilities: Generates, runs and debugs SQL and Python in notebooks and the SQL editor
Builds and maintains Lakeflow/Spark Declarative Pipelines and monitors them for failures
Creates AI/BI dashboards and exploratory analyses from natural language
Agent plans for review before execution, custom instructions, agent skills and MCP connections
Scheduled tasks (Beta) and an agentic converter (Beta) for legacy SQL dialects
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Per Databricks' trust page (the claim that it applies to all tiers is not verified). Databricks does not use prompts, data or responses to train generative foundation models offered to third parties. Partner model providers (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI on Databricks, Anthropic on Databricks) use zero data retention endpoints. All data sent respects Unity Catalog permissions. Traffic uses TLS and workspace data is AES-256 encrypted; customer-managed keys are not verified here. Genie Code is a Designated Service that follows Geo data residency; in-country routing was added in March 2026 for Brazil, Canada, Japan, Korea, Singapore and the UK. The trust page has a section on PHI, PCI, IRAP and FedRAMP data; the compliance security profile requirement is not verified in detail. From July 2026, HIPAA-profile workspaces can use it only with partner-powered AI disabled, so the Databricks-hosted model serves it. By default an AI classifier auto-approves the agent's actions; users can switch to manual approval.
tools.licensing_pricing: No per-seat list price was found. Since 8 July 2026 Genie Code is pay-as-you-go with a per-user monthly free allowance, managed through account budgets. The size of the allowance is not verified. Genie One and Genie Agents are free for users through 31 January 2027 (service principals excluded and billed). It is not bundled with a suite; it requires a Databricks workspace.
tools.integrations: Unity Catalog, Lakeflow, AI/BI dashboards and MLflow. MCP connections are supported; the specific Jira, Confluence and GitHub connectors are not verified. Relevant to dept 49 Data Engineering.
tools.recent_developments: RENAME: Databricks Assistant is now Genie Code (March 2026), with agentic capabilities. Pay-as-you-go billing began 8 July 2026. HIPAA-profile support (partner AI off) and scheduled tasks (Beta) arrived in July 2026. In-country AI routing was added in March 2026.
tools.best_fit_departments: 49 Data Engineering & Data Platforms is a strong fit for SQL generation, pipelines and quality troubleshooting, but only for organisations on Databricks.
tools.training_notes: Learners need Unity Catalog permissions, prompt and plan review, approval modes, and testing of generated code before production. Suggested 24-32 hours (Specialist band).
tools.caveats: Agentic features need partner-powered AI enabled and a supported region. Auto-approve mode can execute code, so choose approval mode deliberately. Databricks warns that output can be wrong. Usage is metered, so cost controls matter.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All ten departments work mostly with long, unstructured, high-stakes documents (board papers, contracts, filings, case files, deal data rooms), so the shared AI pattern is summarise, compare, extract and draft, with a named human accountable for the output. The sources agree on the same controls: use approved enterprise tools, treat outputs as claims to verify (COSO's framing), keep an inventory of use cases, and scale human review to risk. Shared risks are privilege waiver and discoverability of AI transcripts, material non-public information and deal confidentiality, personal data in investigations (GDPR, whistleblower protections), and AI output that cannot be traced for audit or assurance. Evidence is thinnest for Office of the CEO, ERM and Ethics, where findings come from practitioner or vendor pieces rather than studies. Train together on a common module covering data classification, verification and prompt/output logging, with joint labs for Board Secretariat, Legal and Compliance (records and privilege), for Compliance, Internal Audit and ERM (controls evidence and COSO), and for Corporate Strategy and Corporate Development (scenario and deal analysis).

Real-time meeting summaries with agreements, disagreements and suggested actions, so executives can leave a meeting and catch up on return [1]

Drafting and summarising communications and reports, and analysing data in Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel, taught through role-specific 1:1 training at a global manufacturer (the specific apps and tasks are not verified on the opened page) [2]
Drafting a first cut of a difficult conversation or message, which the executive then rewrites in their own voice [1]

Selecting a small number of high-impact use cases tied to business goals, with a roadmap and KPIs, as a CEO-CIO joint task (2023 commentary, background only; page opened, specifics not individually checked) [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A weekly CEO briefing pack for one real (or anonymised) week: a one-page decision brief, a KPI narrative with every figure traced to its source, and a meeting-decision log. Submit the documented prompts, the verification checklist showing each number checked against source, and a measured before/after time log (target: at least 40% reduction against a baseline week). Sized for Core-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Board and strategy papers, unannounced results and deals (material non-public information under securities rules), personal data of executives and staff (GDPR), and privileged legal advice. Rules: use only the licensed enterprise assistant inside the tenant; never paste MNPI into public tools; recorded meetings need consent and a retention rule; the executive office owns verification of every number before it reaches the CEO.
departments.adoption_kpis: Share of executive-office staff using the approved assistant weekly; hours saved per weekly briefing against baseline; share of briefs with all figures source-checked; number of decision-log entries completed within 24 hours of the meeting.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on hands-on drafting and summarising in Microsoft 365 Copilot (the tool leaders actually have in Outlook and Teams), then Claude or Gemini for long-document synthesis, with one short block on verifying numbers. Power BI Copilot only if the office owns KPI dashboards. Concurrency's case shows short, role-specific 1:1 sessions helped executive adoption [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well; Microsoft 365 Copilot is the strongest fit given the cited executive deployments [1][2]. Gamma and ChatGPT Enterprise are optional extras for this function. No opened source names a widely used omitted tool, so omissions are not verified. Source [3] is from 2023, so use it for background only.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: Across the nine departments the dominant pattern is gen AI as a first-draft and synthesis layer (job descriptions, policy answers, feedback and incident summaries, workforce narratives) with a human owning the final decision. The evidence base is mostly vendor and practitioner material: Workday reports a Hackett Group figure that 66% of HR teams use gen AI, but measured outcomes are scarce, so trainees should treat time-saved claims as hypotheses to measure locally. Shared risks are special-category and employee personal data (GDPR), employment-discrimination law, and the EU AI Act and NYC Local Law 144 rules for hiring and worker-management AI, which apply even when a person gives final sign-off. Human reviewers are named as necessary in the payroll and facilities sources; the safety-specific human-review claims (Ibec) could not be verified. Recommended joint training: one common module on employee-data handling, bias testing and human-in-the-loop decisions for departments 11-17 and 19; a second shared lab on HR-knowledge-base prompting for 11, 14, 16 and 18 (employee FAQs, ticket routing); and a safety/facilities pairing for 18 and 19 on incident and work-order summarisation.

departments.name: Human Resources Business Partnering
ai_use_cases: Drafting first-pass answers to common HR inquiries (benefits, leave, payroll, flexible work) from the approved knowledge base, with HR keeping control of final answers [1]
Summarising prior employee cases and conversations so a new HRBP or manager can see history before responding [1]
Producing policy documents, FAQs and manager talking points from HR, legal and compliance input, with human review and sign-off [1]

departments.capstone_deliverable: A manager-guidance pack for one live HR topic (e.g. flexible-work requests): a prompt-built policy Q&A of 15 questions answered only from the approved policy text, each answer checked against the source clause, plus a prompt log and a measured before/after drafting time for 10 cases.
departments.data_risks: Employee relations cases hold health, disciplinary, grievance and family data (GDPR special-category data, employment law, possible legal privilege on advice). Rules: no named case data in non-enterprise tools; anonymise before drafting; answer only from approved policy; HRBP verifies against the policy clause before sending; no AI-generated conclusions on individual performance or discipline.
departments.adoption_kpis: Median drafting time per advisory response vs baseline; share of AI-drafted answers sent with zero factual correction; weekly active users in the HRBP team; policy-answer accuracy in a monthly 20-sample audit; rework rate (drafts discarded).
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Core tier: spend most hours on policy-grounded drafting and verification, then privacy-safe handling of case data. Prioritise Microsoft 365 Copilot (documents and mail where HR already works), Workday AI (case and policy context inside the HCM) and Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise for summarising and drafting. Workday notes that embedded tools reduce silo and governance risk [1].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits. Gemini is plausible where the firm is on Google Workspace. departments.capstone_deliverable: A hiring kit for one real role: bias-checked job description, structured interview guide with scorecard, and an outreach sequence, each with the prompt log, a human-edit record, a bias/credential-inflation checklist result and measured time saved versus the last comparable role.
departments.data_risks: Candidate CVs, contact data, protected characteristics inferred from text, assessment results (GDPR, employment discrimination law). Per Metaview, the EU AI Act high-risk hiring rules start 2 December 2027 for some tools; NYC Local Law 144 is in force now; Colorado's law starts 1 January 2027 but enforcement is on hold under a federal court order; a human final click does not by itself take a tool out of scope [2]. Rules: no ranking or rejection by general chatbots; keep candidate data in approved systems; log tool use; disclose AI use where laws require.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to draft a job description; time-to-shortlist; hiring-manager satisfaction with briefs; proportion of postings passing the inclusive-language checklist; candidate-notice and bias-audit compliance rate for any scoring tool.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Advanced tier: split hours between content generation (JDs, outreach, interview design) and a compliance block on automated decision tools. Prioritise Claude or Gemini for drafting, Workday AI for in-system recruiting, LinkedIn Recruiter AI for sourcing (with an explicit bias-audit lesson), and Microsoft 365 Copilot for scheduling and notes.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit; LinkedIn Recruiter AI is the right sourcing tool but it is the one most likely to be an in-scope automated decision tool, so it needs audit and notice training (general point from [2]; LinkedIn is not named there). Interview-scheduling and candidate-chat assistants are not on the list; Metaview says EU Article 50(1) requires providers (usually the vendor, not the employer) to build in an AI-disclosure since 2 August 2026, so the training should cover vendor checks [2]. Not verified which named vendors the firm uses.

departments.name: Learning & Development
ai_use_cases: Outlining courses, storyboarding, writing learning objectives, generating narration and multimedia; 37% of surveyed designers said AI greatly cut course design time and 70% said it improved quality (232 respondents, sponsor-linked) [1]
AI role-play simulations for practising feedback, coaching and objection-handling conversations [2]
Qualitative analysis of open-ended feedback and survey comments, which rose from 8th to 5th in a 600+ professional L&D survey [2]
Personalised learning paths from skills data and role expectations [3]
Turning long reports and complex policies into short learner-friendly explainers and scenarios [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A 30-minute micro-course on one real topic: learning objectives, 10-question quiz with answer rationale, a facilitator guide and a short visual deck, with every fact traced to a named source document, a prompt log and design hours versus the team's last comparable course.
departments.data_risks: Learner records and assessment results (GDPR), possible health or performance information in feedback comments, and third-party content under copyright. The ATD survey cites trust/accuracy and IP/copyright concerns as reasons designers distrust or avoid AI output [1]. Rules: ground content in approved source documents; fact-check every claim; do not paste confidential material into consumer tools; strip names from feedback before analysis.
departments.adoption_kpis: Design hours per course hour vs baseline; share of courses with AI-assisted drafting; subject-matter-expert review cycles per course; learner satisfaction and quiz pass rate; factual errors found in review.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Core tier: concentrate on grounded content generation and verification. Prioritise NotebookLM (source-grounded study material and quizzes), Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise for objectives and scenarios, and Gamma or Canva Magic Studio for delivery assets. Add a short block on analysing feedback data, since that is the fastest-growing use [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Strong fit: the list covers drafting, grounded sources and visual output. Weak fit: none clearly. Not verified: dedicated learning-platform AI (LMS authoring and skills platforms) is omitted; Workday's page describes personalised paths inside the HCM, so Workday AI is arguably relevant here [3].

departments.name: Compensation, Benefits & Payroll
ai_use_cases: Pre-payroll anomaly checks on time data (missing breaks, overtime clusters, double bookings) and master-data validation; one source gives maturity ratings from high for validation to low for bonuses and severance [1]
A reported 200-employee automotive supplier case: AI caught 94% of time-data errors and cut final payroll errors 78% (unverified, vendor blog) [1]
Employee self-service chatbots answering questions such as why net pay changed, with individual consultation still needed [1]
Matching jobs to market pay data, finding unexplained pay gaps, and modelling merit and budget scenarios, without deciding pay [2]
Pay-equity audits and benchmarking tools used alongside raise-recommendation features in HCM suites [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A payroll-exception review pack for one anonymised monthly dataset: documented prompts to flag anomalies, a reviewer sign-off table showing each flag confirmed or rejected, a pay-gap summary with method notes, and measured review hours saved with false-positive rate.
departments.data_risks: Salary, bank, tax, benefits, health and dependants data (GDPR; payroll and tax law). Compensation AI that suggests individual pay is likely high-risk under the EU AI Act (Annex III point 4(b)) per one legal commentary, and the EU Pay Transparency Directive adds explanation duties [3]. Rules: use only anonymised or synthetic extracts in general tools; aggregate benchmarking differs from per-worker recommendations; never let AI set pay; keep audit trail; human approval of every payment change.
departments.adoption_kpis: Payroll error rate per cycle; time spent on pre-payroll checks; exceptions caught before pay run; share of employee payroll queries resolved in self-service; unexplained pay-gap items closed.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Specialist tier: most hours on accuracy controls, data-protection and evidence, less on generation. Prioritise Workday AI (in-system data), Power BI Copilot (variance and cost analytics), Claude for exception explanation and spreadsheet review, and Microsoft 365 Copilot for employee FAQ drafts. Include a lab on hallucinated numbers.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Fit is reasonable but Gemini adds little specific to payroll. Omitted: dedicated pay-benchmarking and pay-equity tools (Payscale, Ravio, Syndio, Trusaic are named in one commentary) and HCM compensation modules such as SAP SuccessFactors Compensation [3]. Evidence is mostly vendor and legal-adviser commentary.

departments.name: Talent Management & Succession
ai_use_cases: Talent-review summaries consolidating successors, risk and readiness into leadership narratives [1]
Drafting performance review comments and development goals from feedback and goals, as starting points managers refine [1]
Personalised development plans and surfacing adjacent skills and career paths [1]
Skills-gap analysis and internal mobility matching [2]
Task-level work mapping to judge where AI changes roles and succession needs [2]
Adoption is still low: a Deloitte India study of 156 organisations found 9% use AI in succession management and 74% report minimal data use [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A succession and development pack for one anonymised critical role: skills matrix, readiness narrative for three candidate profiles, development pathways, documented prompts and a bias check comparing outputs across demographic variants, plus time saved against the last talent review.
departments.data_risks: Performance ratings, potential assessments, health or leave history, and protected characteristics (GDPR; discrimination law). AI that influences promotion or worker evaluation is in EU AI Act high-risk territory (Annex III point 4) per Praxikon [4]. Rules: no AI-generated potential or readiness ratings used as the decision; managers own judgements; test outputs for demographic skew; restrict access to need-to-know; record where AI informed a decision.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to prepare a talent-review pack; percentage of critical roles with documented successors; manager use of AI-drafted development plans; internal fill rate for critical roles; bias-check completion rate.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Advanced tier: emphasise structured synthesis and fairness testing. Prioritise Workday AI (skills and talent data), Claude (long-document synthesis of review material), Power BI Copilot (pipeline and bench-strength views) and Microsoft 365 Copilot for packaging.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit. Gemini is a duplicate general assistant. Omitted: talent-marketplace and skills platforms (Gloat sells one and SAP SuccessFactors is named as an HCM option) [2]. Source for the omission is a vendor blog, so treat as indicative.

departments.name: People Analytics & HR Operations
ai_use_cases: Natural-language questions on people data returning explanations grounded in live data for non-technical leaders [1]
Explaining why metrics moved (turnover spikes, hiring slowdowns) and drafting workforce summaries for leadership or the board [1]
Comparing workforce scenarios on cost, risk and capacity [1]
Attrition flight-risk scoring paired with manager actions; a cited HP case reports about $300 million savings, from secondary reporting [2]
Hire-success modelling linking interview signals to retention and promotion [2]
Pilot design: one outcome, 6-12 months of data, track attrition, time-to-hire and manager action rate [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A workforce insight brief on an anonymised or synthetic HR dataset: five natural-language queries with validated outputs against a manual calculation, one attrition-pattern analysis with a group-level fairness check, documented prompts, and hours saved versus a manual report.
departments.data_risks: Pseudonymous but re-identifiable HRIS, pay, absence and performance data (GDPR data minimisation, small-cell disclosure, works-council consultation in some countries). The vendor source recommends holdout validation, group-level performance metrics across protected groups, drift detection and periodic recalibration [2]; its claims on minimising features and excluding sensitive attributes were not found and are not verified. Rules: aggregate with minimum group sizes; no individual-level prediction shared outside HR; verify every AI-computed figure against the source.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to produce a monthly workforce report; share of AI-generated figures verified without error; number of leader self-service queries; manager action rate after attrition alerts; forecast accuracy against actual attrition.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Advanced tier: put hours on data validation and fairness testing. Prioritise Power BI Copilot (dashboards and queries), Workday AI (system data), Claude or Gemini (analysis narratives and code assist) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Excel and reporting). The cited sources show attrition models need recalibration and fairness checks [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit. Omitted: dedicated people-analytics platforms such as Visier, named in one source as a workforce-planning case [2]. Vendor-written source (MiHCM); claims such as HP's savings are unverified.

departments.name: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
ai_use_cases: Drafting messages with inclusive language by specifying inclusivity in the prompt [1]
Reviewing existing documents for inclusive language and suggesting edits [1]
Detecting and rewriting biased wording in job descriptions, evaluations and feedback; Intuit built a Slack bot that privately suggests more inclusive phrasing [2]
Supporting neurodivergent colleagues and multilingual communication [2]
Summarising feedback and survey results into themes and recommended actions [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: An inclusive-language review of one real policy or job family: before/after text, a log of each AI suggestion accepted or rejected with rationale, an anonymised feedback theme summary from at least 50 comments, a bias test of AI output, prompts and time saved.
departments.data_risks: Self-identified diversity data and survey comments are special-category data under GDPR (race, religion, health, sexual orientation) and sensitive under equal-opportunity law. A DEI practitioner whitepaper warns that models can reproduce biases from training data and company records, citing Amazon's recruiting tool [4]. Rules: aggregate and anonymise before analysis; minimum group sizes; no inferring protected traits; AI language suggestions are advisory and need human cultural review.
departments.adoption_kpis: Documents reviewed for inclusive language per month; share of AI suggestions accepted after human review; time to synthesise a survey round; coverage of anonymised feedback themes validated by a human reader; reviewer-reported bias incidents in AI output.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Core tier: spend hours on bias recognition in outputs and anonymisation practice. Prioritise Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise (language review and theme synthesis), Microsoft 365 Copilot (in-document edits) and Power BI Copilot (aggregate representation views, only with small-cell rules).
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Mostly fits; Gamma is a weak fit because DEI work is review and analysis, not presentation production. Not verified: no widely used DEI-specific tool is evidenced in the opened sources, so no omission is claimed.

departments.name: Workplace Administration & Facilities
ai_use_cases: Conversational work-order intake: the user describes a problem in chat, the assistant diagnoses it, recommends services and generates the work order; Lessen reports a 20% cut in time to produce a work order and human handling in only 1% of conversations (vendor-reported, 2024). [1]

Portfolio-wide FM platforms that aggregate HVAC, lighting, security and occupancy sensor data into one app so technicians and facility managers see actionable insights (JLL Serve, built on Sclera AI). [2]
Natural-language queries over real estate documents and occupancy, rent and energy metrics, e.g. CBRE's self-service AI playground and its AWS Bedrock prototype. [2]
Enterprise assistants (Azure OpenAI and Copilot for Microsoft 365 at Cushman & Wakefield; JLL GPT) for staff drafting and research. [2]

Backlog clearing: IFMA/JLL webinar frames AI against late work orders, inconsistent vendor performance, re-keyed asset data and spend reporting; it says some use cases pay back faster than others, but no figures were seen. [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Core-tier capstone (about 4-6 hours): a routing and response pack for one facility. Deliver a categorised set of 20 anonymised sample requests with an AI-drafted triage and routing rule table, 3 vendor communication templates, and a Power Automate or ServiceNow flow outline. Include the prompt log, a human check of every routing decision against a manual baseline, and measured minutes saved per request.
departments.data_risks: Handles employee and visitor personal data (access logs, badge and occupancy sensor data, CCTV, accessibility and medical-related requests), vendor contracts and pricing, and building security details. Rules: no personal data or security layouts in non-enterprise tools; anonymise tickets before prompting; treat occupancy and sensor analytics as employee monitoring subject to GDPR and local employment law; human approval before spend commitments or vendor instructions. The sources do not detail these rules, so they are standard practice, not claims from the pages.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time from request to work order created; share of requests auto-routed correctly without rework (target set against a baseline); work-order backlog and overdue count; vendor first-time-fix or SLA compliance; weekly active users of the approved AI tool among facilities staff.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Core tier: spend hours on prompt basics for ticket triage and vendor emails, plus workflow automation. Prioritise Microsoft 365 Copilot (drafting, summarising), Power Automate (routing flows) and ServiceNow Now Assist (ticket classification and summaries, if the firm runs it). Gemini is a general fallback. Teach redaction and verification.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well for ticket and routing work. Canva Magic Studio is a weak fit: none of the opened sources describe design tools in facilities work, so it suits only signage and event materials. The list omits CAFM/CMMS-embedded assistants that sources show are the main FM tools, such as JLL Serve and Lessen Copilot, and building-intelligence tools such as VergeSense (Workplace Assistant) and BrainBox AI named in [1]. These are vendor or trade-press sources.

departments.name: Health, Safety & Wellbeing
ai_use_cases: Drafting and reviewing safety statements, risk assessments and procedures with generative AI, with review by a competent person. [1]
Generating scenario-based safety training modules and quizzes tailored to a workforce. [1][2]
Summarising incident reports and spotting patterns; advisory only, not a replacement for formal risk analysis. [1]
Enhanced incident reporting with real-time risk detection, e.g. a virtual risk assistant tested in workplaces in Estonia, and predictive risk modelling in heavy manufacturing and insurance. [2]
Generating machine and equipment safety instructions from risk assessment and job hazard data, and recording incidents, near misses and observations on mobile (SAP EHS, vendor documentation). [3]
Computer vision on existing CCTV for site safety (behavioural safety, PPE detection) with agentic reporting for EHS teams (Protex, vendor material, not independently verified). [4]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Advanced-tier capstone (about 8-12 hours): an AI-assisted safety pack for one task or site. Deliver a job hazard checklist and a toolbox-talk or training module with quiz, plus a summary of 10 anonymised incident narratives with themes. Include the prompt log, a competent-person sign-off sheet recording every correction to AI output, source checks against the applicable regulation, and time saved versus manual drafting.
departments.data_risks: Handles health and injury data, incident narratives naming workers, wellbeing and occupational health records, and CCTV footage. Regulatory hooks: GDPR (Ibec says no confidential or health-related data should go into AI tools unless anonymised and secured), the EU AI Act (transparency and mandatory human oversight) and, in Ireland, the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005, under which legal responsibility stays with the human competent person. [1] Outside the EU, equivalents such as HIPAA and OSHA recordkeeping would apply (not covered by the sources). AI predictions are advisory only.
departments.adoption_kpis: Hours to produce a risk assessment or training module versus baseline; share of AI-drafted documents passing competent-person review without major correction; incident report completion time and near-miss reporting volume; number of trained EHS staff using approved tools; count of data-handling breaches or redaction failures (target zero).
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Advanced tier: emphasise verification and governance over generation. Prioritise Claude or Gemini for drafting and incident summarisation (long-document handling), Microsoft 365 Copilot for documents inside the tenant, and Power BI Copilot for incident trend dashboards. Gamma only for training decks. Teach anonymisation, citing the regulation, and challenging AI summaries; the NSC review notes limited AI literacy and scepticism among EHS professionals and a need for clean, structured data. [2]
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list suits drafting, training material and trend analysis. Gamma is a weak fit for safety-critical work, as the sources show no use beyond presentation of content. The handbook omits EHS-platform assistants that the sources show are an embedded route: SAP EHS with Joule [3], and computer-vision platforms such as Protex [4]. These are vendor materials, so claims are unverified.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All eight departments turn structured ledger, bank, spend or contract data into drafts, summaries and exception lists that a named human then reviews, so the shared skill is verification: reperforming numbers, tying output to source and documenting who signed off. Shared risks are confident-but-wrong output, material non-public information, personal and bank data, and weak evidence trails; sources describe COSO's February 2026 generative-AI control guidance and a Workiva finding that 1 in 4 executives said an AI error reached investors or the board. Microsoft itself warns against relying on Copilot in Excel for finance decisions. Training should be joint for a common core (data classification, review gates, prompt and evidence logging) and for three pairings: FP&A, Accounting and Treasury (variance, forecast and close narratives in spreadsheets); AP, Procurement and Vendor Management (P2P documents, contracts, supplier data and fraud signals); and FP&A with Investor Relations (earnings numbers and narrative consistency). Tax and IR need their own legal and disclosure modules.

departments.name: Financial Planning & Analysis
ai_use_cases: Drafting first-pass variance commentary from ledger detail with an LLM; the analyst checks every claim because drafts sound equally confident when wrong [1].

Natural-language questions on planning data inside an FP&A platform (for example 'why did Q2 revenue drop in EMEA?') returning data-backed explanations for monthly business reviews and board books [2].
Running multiple what-if scenarios (inflation, tariffs, supply shifts) on driver-based models in minutes instead of days, with analysts owning assumptions [1][2].
Drafting management reports by department or cost centre against budget from a trial balance, then having analysts add interpretation [3].
Baseline statistical or ML forecasts refreshed each cycle; one source cautions that simple statistical methods have beaten ML in published tests, so baselines are a starting point [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A one-month variance pack for a sanitized or synthetic cost-centre dataset: AI-drafted commentary on the top 10 variances, each claim tied to a ledger line, plus a scenario table (base, downside, upside) with stated driver assumptions. Submit the documented prompts, the verification log showing corrections made to AI output, and measured time against a manual baseline. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unreleased results and forecasts are material non-public information for listed companies (securities law, insider-trading and Reg FD exposure). Budgets carry compensation and headcount detail (employment law, GDPR if staff-identifiable). Rules: use only enterprise-licensed tools with no training on inputs, anonymise employee-level data, keep forecast files off consumer tools, keep a human reviewer on any number that leaves finance. Microsoft's Copilot in Excel FAQ says to avoid using Copilot for decisions in sensitive areas such as finance and to verify output [4]. AFP respondents cited data reliability (61%) as a barrier [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Share of FP&A staff using approved AI weekly (AFP benchmark: 23% use AI daily, weekly or monthly) [1]; hours to produce monthly variance commentary versus baseline; percentage of AI-drafted claims corrected at review; forecast error by horizon before and after; number of scenarios run per planning cycle.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on hands-on variance commentary and scenario work with verification routines, then governance. Prioritise Excel Copilot (where the models live), Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise for narrative and long-document reasoning, and Power BI Copilot for natural-language data exploration. Teach reperformance of every number, because outputs read as authoritative even when wrong [1][4].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well: Excel Copilot, Power BI Copilot and a general LLM cover the core jobs. Gemini and ChatGPT Enterprise overlap; one general assistant plus the Microsoft tools is enough for most teams (judgment). Omitted: dedicated planning platforms with embedded generative AI, such as OneStream SensibleAI, which offers narrative variance summaries and natural-language questions inside the planning model [2].

departments.name: Accounting & Financial Reporting
ai_use_cases: Describing a transaction in plain English and having GenAI draft a multi-line journal entry against the chart of accounts, turning data entry into review and approval [1].
Uploading bank and ledger datasets so the model identifies matches, discrepancies and unrecorded items, then drafting control-account reconciliation summaries [1].
Estimating accruals for services received but not yet invoiced from an anonymised service contract, with accountant review [1]; SAP has released an Accounting Accruals Agent in Joule [3].
Variance analysis on a trial balance with first-draft commentary and draft footnote disclosures from supplied data and the relevant standard [1].
Close agents that prepare reconciliations and draft journals for human sign-off, from vendors such as BlackLine and FloQast [2].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A month-end mini-close on synthetic data: five reconciliations and three journal entries drafted with AI, plus draft variance commentary. Deliver a control memo covering agent scope and named owner, retained inputs and reasoning, reviewer sign-off per item, error rate found on review, and measured time saved against manual preparation. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unpublished financial statements (material non-public information), data feeding financial reporting under SOX internal control over financial reporting, and supplier, customer and employee personal data inside ledgers (GDPR). Rules: every AI output feeding the statements needs a human approval step scaled to materiality; keep an inventory of AI tools with a named owner; retain inputs, steps, exceptions and match basis so a reviewer or auditor can replay them; check SOC reports for what they say about AI components [2]. COSO issued guidance on internal control over generative AI in February 2026 [2]. Anonymise contracts before upload [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Days to close; percentage of reconciliations AI-prepared and passed at first review; reviewer-found error rate on AI drafts (set an exit threshold, as recommended) [2]; manual journal entry preparation hours; share of AI tools with a documented owner and evidence standard [2].
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Weight hours to controls and review, then to close tasks. Prioritise Excel Copilot (reconciliations, variance on trial balances), SAP Joule (where SAP is the ledger, for accruals and embedded agents), and Claude or Microsoft 365 Copilot for contract reading and journal explanations. Vendor match-rate claims are marketing until your own data reproduces them [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Fit is good for ERP-centred teams: Excel Copilot and SAP Joule match the work, and Joule applies only if the company runs SAP [3]. Gemini adds little beyond Claude and Microsoft 365 Copilot in a Microsoft shop (judgment). Omitted: dedicated close and reconciliation platforms such as BlackLine and FloQast, plus Microsoft's Dynamics 365 reconciliation agent in preview [2].

departments.name: Treasury & Cash Management
ai_use_cases: Cash flow forecasting from daily bank balances plus open receivables and payables, producing a baseline and range and showing which regions miss most, so the treasurer reviews misses rather than collecting files [2].
FX exposure mapping: reading open invoices and purchase orders into currencies and settlement dates and refreshing a net exposure report daily; hedge decisions stay human [2].
Payment fraud screening that flags changed bank details and scores payments against vendor history, with independent release and call-back controls [2].
Drafting a daily cash position note from bank statements, with reviewer tie-out to bank balances [2].

Generative AI for cash positioning: Deloitte's 2024 survey of 213 organisations found over 70% saw cash forecasting, and 50% cash positioning, as the most impactful use cases (as summarised by HighRadius) [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A 13-week cash forecast pack on synthetic multi-currency data: AI-assisted baseline and range, a back-test of forecast error against actuals by horizon, a net FX exposure table, and a one-page position note. Include documented prompts, a rule list of what the tool may never do (move money, commit hedges), and time saved. Sized for Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Bank account numbers and credentials, payment instructions, covenant and liquidity positions (often material non-public information), counterparty data, and card data if in scope (PCI DSS). Business email compromise affected 74% of US organisations in AFP's 2026 payments fraud survey [2]. Rules: no bank details or credentials in prompts; AI never releases payments or changes bank mandates; dual authorisation and call-back for account changes [2]; treat AI-generated hedge or funding suggestions as drafts under the treasury policy. AFP's 2026 benchmarking survey scored AI and emerging-technology policies lowest of any treasury policy area [2], so write one first.
departments.adoption_kpis: Forecast error by horizon versus pre-AI baseline (only 18% rated their forecasting capability above average or best in class in Deloitte's survey) [1]; hours spent assembling the weekly forecast; share of forecast files received via automated feed rather than spreadsheet; fraud flags raised and confirmed; policy exceptions logged.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Specialist hours should go to forecasting accuracy measurement and payment-control design. Prioritise Excel Copilot for scenario and position work, Power BI Copilot for liquidity reporting, and Claude for reading bank, loan and covenant documents. Include a controls module on never letting AI release funds [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Partial fit. Excel Copilot and Power BI Copilot suit reporting, but Microsoft advises avoiding Excel Copilot for decisions in sensitive areas such as finance [3]. Gemini and ChatGPT Enterprise are generic and weaker for forecasting, which sources describe with ML or predictive tools [2]. Omitted: treasury management systems and dedicated cash-forecasting tools, such as HighRadius cash forecasting and the TMS layer, which Deloitte links to cash positioning [1].
