departments.name: Taxation
ai_use_cases: Tax research: LLMs summarise complex regulations, provide precedents and answer specific queries [2]; tax research was the top GenAI use case (77%) in the Thomson Reuters Institute 2025 survey [1].
Extracting data from unstructured invoices, contracts and regulatory filings to cut manual entry [2].
Drafting first versions of tax memos, reports and responses to tax authorities for professional review [2].
Modelling tax planning scenarios from historical data and current rules to estimate financial impact [2].
Document summarisation (55%) and document review (53%) are also among top use cases in the same survey [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A research memo on a defined, public-fact tax question (for example a VAT treatment of a cross-border service), with every authority cited and verified against the primary source, plus a structured extraction of key fields from five sample invoices. Submit prompts, a citation verification table, an error log and time saved. Sized for Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Taxpayer identifiers, employee and shareholder data (GDPR), transfer-pricing and planning positions that are commercially sensitive and may attract legal privilege if prepared with counsel, and unfiled results (material non-public information). Rules: cite and verify every authority since accuracy and reliability are the main reservations among tax professionals [1]; keep privileged advice inside approved, access-controlled tools; set governance for data security, access controls and audit trails as the insightsoftware guide recommends [2]; never let AI submit filings. Confirm local rules on tax-data handling with counsel (not verified in sources).
departments.adoption_kpis: Research hours per query versus baseline; share of AI-cited authorities verified correct; documents processed per hour with extraction accuracy; percentage of GenAI users using it at least weekly (73% of tax-firm and 69% of corporate tax users in the 2025 survey) [1]; whether ROI is measured at all, since only 20% of professionals surveyed do [1].
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend hours on research verification and extraction QA. Prioritise Thomson Reuters CoCounsel (grounded tax research; not verified in opened sources), Claude for long-document reading and memo drafting, and Excel Copilot for scenario and reconciliation work. Teach hallucinated-citation checks first.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit: a research-grade tool such as CoCounsel (not verified in opened sources) with general LLMs for drafting. Gemini is generic and weaker for authoritative research (judgment). Omitted: tax-technology suites with embedded AI, such as ONESOURCE (Thomson Reuters) and insightsoftware's Longview Tax, both named in the opened pages [1][2].

departments.name: Accounts Payable & Receivable
ai_use_cases: Extracting, classifying and validating fields from unstructured invoice PDFs with Azure AI Document Intelligence, with human-in-the-loop exception handling; a vendor-reported three-month healthcare proof of concept claimed over 70% field accuracy and about 60% less processing time (self-reported, no baseline disclosed) [1].
Joule helping employees outside AP submit invoices from SAP Cloud ERP with minimal input, feeding procure-to-pay [2].
Receipt analysis and expense checks: SAP Concur Verify inspects receipt images and metadata to flag likely AI-generated receipts [2].
Payment-fraud screening that flags changed supplier bank details and scores payments against vendor history, with call-back controls [3].
Drafting collection follow-ups and supplier queries on exceptions, always sent after human review (judgment, not source-verified).
departments.capstone_deliverable: An exception-handling playbook tested on 30 synthetic invoices (price mismatch, missing PO, duplicate, changed bank details): AI extraction plus a triage table recommending approve, query supplier or escalate, with accuracy scored against an answer key. Submit prompts, extraction error rates, escalation rules and time saved. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Supplier bank details and tax IDs, customer payment data (PCI DSS if card data is present), employee expense data (GDPR), and entries that feed SOX-relevant controls. Rules: never place bank account numbers in general chat tools; changes to supplier bank details need independent call-back [3]; AI extraction runs inside governed systems with exception queues; keep human approval gates scaled to risk and retain evidence for audit [4]. Invoice extraction accuracy of just over 70% in one vendor-reported pilot shows validation is non-optional [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Straight-through processing rate; exception rate and average exception resolution time; duplicate or fraudulent payments caught; extraction field accuracy on a sampled audit; cost per invoice and days sales outstanding for AR follow-up.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Hours go to exception triage and fraud awareness. Prioritise SAP Joule (for SAP shops), Power Automate for routing, and Claude or Gemini for reading messy invoices and drafting supplier replies. Practise sampling extraction output against source documents [1][4].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Fit is reasonable. SAP Joule only applies to SAP customers [2]; Power Automate suits workflow, not judgment. Omitted: dedicated invoice capture and AP automation (the pilot used Azure AI Document Intelligence) [1] and ERP-native tools. Claude and Gemini are secondary for extraction at volume (judgment).

departments.name: Procurement & Strategic Sourcing
ai_use_cases: Drafting RFP and RFQ structure, standard clauses and evaluation criteria from past events, compressing two to three days of drafting into hours of review (vendor claim) [2].
Summarising supplier contracts to surface liability caps, auto-renewal and termination terms so procurement can triage before legal review [2].
Turning spend-analytics data into written narratives for quarterly reviews, for example explaining a logistics spend rise by carrier [2].
Bid analysis comparing supplier bids on total cost including unit price, shipping and payment terms; SAP's Joule bid analysis agent was announced for Q1 2026 [3].

Spend analytics and PO processing are among the areas with most immediate impact; 47% of organisations use embedded GenAI features such as Coupa AI Classification and SAP Joule, and 30% rely on custom-built or general-purpose tools like Microsoft Copilot [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A sourcing event pack for a mock category: AI-drafted RFP, weighted evaluation criteria, a supplier comparison matrix from three sample bids, and a spend narrative from an anonymised spend cube. Each claim is traced to bid or spend data, with documented prompts, an IP and confidentiality check, and time saved. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Supplier pricing and bids (commercially confidential, possibly covered by NDAs), contract terms, negotiating positions, and personal data of supplier contacts (GDPR). Hackett reports data quality, privacy and intellectual property risks as leading challenges [1]. Rules: keep bids and pricing inside approved tools with no training on inputs; never feed one bidder's data into a response that reaches another; have legal review non-standard clauses rather than relying on AI summaries [2]; keep an audit trail of award rationale.
departments.adoption_kpis: RFP drafting cycle time; share of sourcing events using AI-drafted templates; spend under management or classification coverage; contract review turnaround; user-reported productivity gain (Hackett reports a weighted average of 9.9% among early adopters) [1].
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Hours go to RFP drafting, bid comparison and spend narrative, with confidentiality rules. Prioritise Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise (document drafting and contract summaries), SAP Joule where Ariba or SAP is used [3], and Microsoft 365 Copilot for category reports. Include a checkpoint where a person validates every extracted clause.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Mostly fits. Perplexity is a weaker fit for confidential bid work because it is web-search oriented; it suits public supplier and market research (judgment). Omitted: source-to-pay suites with embedded AI, notably Coupa AI Classification and SAP Joule bid analysis [1][3], and spend-analytics platforms such as Simfoni [2].

departments.name: Vendor & Third-Party Management
ai_use_cases: Reviewing AI and security questionnaires against a use-case-based checklist (what data goes into prompts, whether the vendor trains on it, which model providers and subprocessors are involved) [1].
Summarising vendor contracts to find data-use, training, retention and incident-response terms [1]; FINRA suggests contract language barring sensitive data from vendors' open-source GenAI tools [2].
Inventorying embedded AI in purchased software and foundation-model dependencies, asking vendors whether they use GenAI [2].
Policy retrieval and summarisation across vendor policies, which FINRA observed as common GenAI uses [2].
Building supplier performance summaries and scorecard narratives from SLA data (judgment, not source-verified; the Simfoni page was not found to cover SLA scorecards).
departments.capstone_deliverable: A third-party risk file for one mock AI-enabled vendor: AI-assisted questionnaire review, contract-term extraction, risk tier and approval conditions (approved use case, data allowed, monitoring), and a one-page SLA scorecard. Submit prompts, a human-verified findings table and time saved. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Vendor security reports, SOC reports, pricing and contract terms (confidentiality clauses), personal data in questionnaire responses (GDPR), and in regulated firms third-party risk obligations such as FINRA supervision rules [2]. Rules: a vendor can pass a standard security review and still create AI governance risk, so assess by use case [1]; do not upload vendors' confidential security artefacts to unapproved tools; require human sign-off on risk tiers; track fourth parties and subprocessors [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to complete a vendor risk assessment; percentage of vendors with AI usage declared and risk-tiered; share of contracts with data-use and training clauses checked; open findings aging; SLA breaches detected per quarter.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Hours go to AI vendor due diligence and contract extraction, with scorecard reporting second. Prioritise Claude (long contract and report reading), ServiceNow Now Assist (where the vendor register sits; not verified in opened sources), and Power BI Copilot for scorecards. Teach evaluating vendors' own AI by use case [1].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Moderate fit. ServiceNow Now Assist is right if the vendor workflow runs on ServiceNow (not verified in opened sources). Gemini and Microsoft 365 Copilot are generic. First-draft prepared remarks from a bot trained on a CFO's past public remarks, which the CFO then red-lines (Expensify's in-house tool) [2].
Competitive intelligence and peer benchmarking: analysing how peers discuss topics such as FX in their disclosures [1][2].
Compliance support for regulatory disclosure review before release [1].

Anticipating more complex investor questions as analysts use AI themselves; at least 35% of CFOs polled by Gartner reported higher volume, frequency and urgency of investor communications in 2025 versus 2024 [2].
departments.capstone_deliverable: An earnings-prep kit built on a public company's already-released results: AI-generated list of 25 analyst questions ranked by difficulty, draft answers checked against filed figures, a peer-language comparison, and a Reg FD-style review checklist. Submit prompts, a source-verification table, items AI got wrong and time saved. Use only public data. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unreleased earnings, guidance and strategic plans are material non-public information; Regulation FD bars selective disclosure, and the 2005 Flowserve action cited the IR officer alongside the CEO [3]. Rules: AI never decides what is material or compliant; use only enterprise tools with no training on inputs; draft Q&A inside the restricted insider list; legal and disclosure committee review before anything external; one in four executives surveyed by Workiva (2026 mid-year report) said an AI-generated error had reached investors or the board [2]. Consistency with filed numbers must be checked by a person.
departments.adoption_kpis: Hours of earnings-prep time versus prior quarter; share of analyst questions on the call that were anticipated in the AI-assisted Q&A; number of numeric or factual errors caught before release; percentage of drafts passing disclosure-committee review at first pass; AI usage logged per release cycle.

Prioritise Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise for question generation and drafting, Microsoft 365 Copilot for working within Excel and PowerPoint source files, and Power BI Copilot for KPI narratives. Include a module on MNPI and the review chain.

deptClusters.verification_notes: I opened and checked 17 cited pages, including every cited page except the CPA Practice Advisor article's later sections. Statistics and named capabilities matched their sources: COSO February 2026, Workiva 1 in 4, Gartner 35%, Flowserve, AFP 74% BEC and 2.9/5 AI policy score, Hackett 47%/9.9%, TR Institute percentages, SAP Joule/Concur Verify/Bid Analysis, and the Aeries pilot. Corrections were mostly wording precision, plus flags on three tool claims no opened page supports (CoCounsel, Now Assist, Perplexity/Gamma judgments). Overall reliability is good, but the Aeries pilot and Hackett/Simfoni figures are vendor-reported.
removed_or_corrected: FP&A: Microsoft quote corrected to the FAQ's actual wording ('avoid using Copilot for decisions in sensitive areas such as finance'); AFP 23% corrected to 'daily, weekly or monthly'; confidence raised to high after sources confirmed.
Accounting: confidence raised to high; all claims confirmed on ICAEW, CPA Practice Advisor and SAP pages.

Treasury: the Deloitte 70%/50% figures are 'most impactful use cases', not explicitly labelled GenAI, so 'GenAI' was removed; the 18% figure was corrected to 'above average or best in class'; the AI-policy 'lowest' claim was attributed to AFP's 2026 benchmarking survey; Microsoft wording corrected.

Tax: CoCounsel capability could not be verified on any opened page, so it is marked not verified; the weekly-use stat was clarified as 'among GenAI users'; the 20% ROI stat was clarified as 'surveyed'; the reliability reservation was reworded to 'accuracy and reliability'; the audit-trail claim was reworded to 'governance for data security, access controls and audit trails'.
AP/AR: the Aeries pilot was labelled vendor-reported in data_risks.

Procurement: the Hackett 30% was reworded to 'custom-built or general-purpose tools'; 'SAP Ariba capabilities' was changed to SAP Joule bid analysis, because the Ariba claim is not supported by the cited pages; 9.9% was attributed to early adopters; 'most immediate impact' was softened to 'among the areas'.

Vendor management: the FS-ISAC/NIST AI RMF reference was removed because it came from unopened search results; ServiceNow Now Assist was marked not verified; the SLA scorecard use case was flagged because the Simfoni page does not cover it; the Simfoni source was removed from the department's sources and the markers renumbered.

IR: the Gartner stat was completed ('volume, frequency and urgency'); the Workiva claim was attributed to the 2026 mid-year report via Bloomberg Tax; the AlphaSense and Workiva tool-fit claims were reworded to what the pages show; confidence raised to high.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All eight departments use AI for the same core jobs: research and synthesis, personalised first drafts, call and meeting summarisation, and reporting on CRM or campaign data. Sellers and marketers also report that data quality, not the model, is the limiting factor (Salesforce: 74% of AI-using sales teams prioritise data hygiene). Shared risks are personal data of prospects and contacts (UK/EU GDPR, PECR or e-privacy marketing consent), recorded-call consent (wiretap litigation against AI notetakers), confidential pipeline, pricing and customer data, and unverified AI claims reaching buyers. Vendor-reported gains are large but self-reported, and independent analyses of ad automation are more mixed, so training should teach measuring incremental results against a baseline. Train together on a common module covering CRM data hygiene, consent and recording rules, citation-checked research and a human review gate before external sending. Sales Ops with the two sales teams, Marketing with Digital Marketing, and Research with BD and Pre-Sales are natural pairings for hands-on labs.

departments.name: Sales - Enterprise & Key Accounts
ai_use_cases: Account and prospect research summarised from CRM, web and internal data; sellers expect agents to cut research time by 34% once fully implemented (survey of 4,050 sellers) [1]
Call summaries, next-step capture and multi-threading checks: Gong Labs found multi-threaded deals over $50K have 130% higher win rates, so AI flags single-threaded deals [2]
Meeting prep and at-risk deal queries in a copilot grounded in CRM, email and decks, e.g. 'a list of deals that are at risk of falling through' [4]
Professional-services firm pilot: early Copilot users reported about 3 hours saved per week, with CRM-based opportunity use cases [3]
Personalised outreach drafts reviewed by the rep; Salesforce reports agents contacted 130,000 leads and created 3,200 opportunities in four months [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: One strategic-account plan for a real or anonymised key account: AI-assisted account brief with every fact linked to a validated source, a stakeholder map flagging single-threaded risk, a call-summary-to-next-steps workflow, a prompt log, and a time-saved comparison (manual vs AI-assisted, minutes per task). Sized for Core-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Customer confidential data, pricing, contract terms and pipeline are commercially sensitive; contact data is personal data under GDPR/UK GDPR. Call recordings need participant consent and notice: AI notetakers face wiretap-law class actions (federal and state wiretapping laws; e.g. Brewer v. Otter.ai, N.D. Cal. 2025) [5]. Rules: use only the enterprise-approved tool, announce recording, no pasting named customer data into consumer chatbots, human review before anything is sent.
departments.adoption_kpis: Weekly active AI users per rep; minutes spent on pre-call research and CRM updates (before vs after); share of opportunities with 3+ buyer contacts; calls recorded with consent notice logged (%); follow-up email turnaround time.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on account research with citation checks, call-summary workflows, and CRM-grounded prompting. Prioritise Salesforce Einstein and Gong AI because they work on the CRM and call data sellers already use; Microsoft 365 Copilot for email and meeting prep; Claude for synthesis. Teach consent and verification explicitly; Gartner-style reinvestment of saved time is a manager topic.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit overall: Einstein, Gong and Copilot match the cited use cases [1][2][4]. Gamma is a weak fit for core selling work (deck output, not research or CRM). Omission: AI meeting notetakers such as Otter and Fireflies are widely used and Otter is the subject of 2025 consent litigation, so the handbook should name the approved recorder and ban unapproved bots [5]. Sales agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot connect to Dynamics 365 and Salesforce, relevant if the firm is on either CRM [4]. Einstein and Gong capabilities beyond the cited pages: not verified.

departments.tool_fit_commentary: Google Ads AI and Advantage+ fit, but both are opaque and platform-reported numbers can differ from true acquisition cost [2]; Pixis is one vendor selling independent measurement and is not listed (it is itself a vendor) [2]. Per Xpert.Digital, Google will discontinue Dynamic Search Ads as a standalone format and migrate campaigns to AI Max (postponed to February 2027), so AI Max should be added [1]. Gamma is a weak fit. Claude is not listed though used for ad copy [3].

Early-stage market briefings validated by analysts: Latham's research team reports a better product in the same time, not mainly time saved [2]

AI adoption in competitive intelligence is accelerating but held back by data quality, privacy and expertise concerns (109-respondent life sciences survey) [4]
Recurring monitoring prompts reused for single-company research [2]

departments.data_risks: Survey and panel data can contain personal data (GDPR); competitor intelligence must be gathered lawfully (no misrepresentation or breach of confidentiality, trade-secret and competition-law limits; not verified on an opened page); client research may be under NDA. departments.adoption_kpis: Share of claims with verified sources; turnaround time for a briefing; stakeholder satisfaction score; number of recurring monitors running; hallucination or correction rate found in review.

Co-sell routing: AI predicts which partners can influence a deal and suggests introductions, replacing manual deal registration [1]. Futurum also reports AWS and Dell using algorithms to select co-sell partners [2].

Partner operations agents for onboarding, partner portals, demo environments and deal registration, reported by Futurum from vendor briefings at AWS, Dell, Google Cloud, IBM, Lenovo, Salesforce and ServiceNow [2].

Generative AI drafts partner-specific one-pagers and outreach; an unnamed software company in a consultancy snapshot saw more opportunities with an engaged partner and better co-sell win rates (anecdotal, unquantified) [1].
Systematic partner prospecting and outreach, with a data-enrichment tool (Clay) feeding an AI qualification and messaging tool (Octave) (vendor how-to, unverified results) [4].

Partner targeting is shifting: IDC reports partner value moving toward AI solution design, governance and compliance services and industry advisory [3]. That this should change which partners BD targets is an inference, not stated by IDC.

It contains 5 ranked candidate partners with cited fit rationale, a relationship map, a one-page joint proposal, and a prompt log with time saved against a manual baseline. A reviewer checks that every firmographic or market claim traces to a validated source. About 4 hours at Core tier.
departments.data_risks: Partner and prospect commercial terms, pricing, pipeline and NDA-covered material, plus contact personal data (GDPR/CCPA for outreach and relationship mapping). Do not paste NDA or deal-registration data into unapproved tools. Check lawful basis before profiling individuals. Verify AI-sourced partner facts before they appear in proposals. Any shared multi-party data needs agreed data-sharing policies [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to identify and shortlist partners vs baseline; partner activation rate; share of opportunities with an engaged partner; co-sell win rate and deal velocity; proposal turnaround time [1].

departments.name: Pre-Sales & Solution Consulting
ai_use_cases: Security questionnaire automation: reviewers edit AI drafts from an approved content library; Fiddler AI cut a 30-hour questionnaire to 3-4 hours (87%), vendor-reported [1].
RFP first drafts at scale: SugarAI reports 90% of initial response work automated and roughly 12-18 questions per RFP still routed to SMEs, vendor-reported [2].
Freeing solution consultants from searching and drafting so they focus on solution strategy and customer engagement (SugarAI's Director, Solution Consulting) [2].
Personalised demos: AI tailors demo messaging by persona and topic and cuts demo creation from days to minutes (vendor claim) [3].
Prospect-specific demo data: a tool generates demo records from a discovery call and injects them into the live app (vendor page) [4].
Conversation intelligence on discovery and demo calls to surface objections and improve demo prep [3].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A response-and-demo kit for one realistic RFP excerpt (at least 25 questions): AI-drafted answers each tagged with an approved source or flagged for SME review, a tailored solution proposal outline, and a demo script with persona-specific talking points. Include a prompt log and measured time saved against a manual baseline. About 8 hours at Advanced tier; assessed on factual accuracy and correct flagging of unsupported claims.
departments.data_risks: Customer confidential data, pricing, unreleased roadmap, security architecture details and NDA material. RFP answers can become contractual commitments, so unverified AI claims about security, compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR) or features create legal exposure. Rules: draft only from approved content, route technical and legal claims to SMEs, never paste customer data into unapproved tools, and keep a human sign-off. Frequent hallucinations (plus missing workflow features) led Fiddler to replace its homegrown chatbot [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Hours per RFP or questionnaire vs baseline; share of answers needing minimal edits; RFPs answered per headcount; SME minutes per response; demo prep time [1][2].
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Advanced tier: put most hours on grounded drafting with citations, review workflows and demo preparation. Prioritise Claude (long RFP documents and structured drafts), Microsoft 365 Copilot (internal content and meeting notes), Salesforce Einstein (opportunity context) and Gamma (proposal and demo decks). Teach SME routing and claim verification.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list is general-purpose and omits dedicated RFP and questionnaire platforms (AutoRFP.ai is evidenced in [1][2]; Loopio and Responsive were not opened, so not verified) and demo platforms (Demoboost [3], Reprise [4]). Gong is listed by a vendor article as a presales tool [3] but is not on this department's list. Salesforce Einstein fits opportunity context but no presales-specific evidence was found for it. deptClusters.cluster_overview: All five departments turn unstructured customer signals (tickets, calls, surveys, interview notes, feedback, usage data) into summaries, drafts and prioritised actions, and in each one the tool's output is a draft that a human must validate. The shared risks are customer personal data (GDPR/UK GDPR), unapproved "shadow AI" use, and confident but wrong output. Wrong output includes misread sentiment, invented user insight and mis-scored churn risk. Vendor-reported results (resolution rates, retention gains) are marketing claims and should not be used as training benchmarks. Customer Success, Support and CX should train together on voice-of-customer synthesis, data handling and human escalation rules. Product Management and Product Design & UX Research should train together on evidence-grounded PRDs, research synthesis and acceptance criteria. A joint cross-cluster session could use one shared feedback dataset, taking it from support tickets to themes to backlog items.

departments.name: Customer Success
ai_use_cases: Continuous account health monitoring: an AI agent in the CRM combines product adoption, usage velocity, support case frequency, executive engagement and contract milestones, flags anomalies and proposes actions to the CSM (tool type: CRM-embedded agent; outcome: earlier renewal-risk detection, consultancy-described, not measured) [1]
Next-best-action drafting: the agent recommends outreach, content to share or internal escalation, for example a technical enablement session for an account struggling with advanced features [1]
Routine task automation: renewal reminders, health-check emails and meeting preparation partially automated by AI so CSMs spend time on high-impact accounts [1]
Meeting-derived sentiment: a Gainsight customer-story page reportedly adds meeting-summary data to sentiment scoring (page could not be opened, not verified)
Support-signal enrichment: support-case frequency and resolution time are fed into the account profile so CSMs see service friction before a renewal conversation [1]
CX benchmark context for CS conversations: Zendesk reports 22% higher customer retention among 'CX Trendsetters' (vendor survey, treat as indicative) [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A renewal-risk brief pack for 5 anonymised or synthetic accounts. For each account: a Claude or Gemini draft health summary, a human-corrected risk rating with evidence, a success plan, and a renewal email draft. Submit with the prompt log, a source/validation table (every claim traced to a CRM field or call note) and measured time saved against a manual baseline. Sized for about 12-16 Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Customer contact details, contract values and pricing, usage telemetry, support transcripts and stakeholder names. GDPR/UK GDPR applies to named contacts and call notes (lawful basis, minimisation, DPIA for profiling). Contracts often carry confidentiality clauses. Rules: use only enterprise-approved tools; strip personal data when pasting outside the CRM; never let AI send customer-facing messages or alter commercial terms without human review; keep customer data in the CRM's governed agent where possible. Zendesk reports shadow AI use (external tools unapproved for agent use) jumping up to 250% year on year in some industries and links this to privacy, security and service-quality risk [2].
departments.adoption_kpis: Share of at-risk accounts flagged at least 60 days before renewal; CSM prep time per QBR/renewal (minutes); percentage of AI-drafted outreach edited and approved versus rejected; gross revenue retention on accounts using AI health review versus control; weekly active AI users among CSMs.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on account research and synthesis, health-signal interpretation, and drafting with human review, with a short module on data handling. Prioritise Salesforce Einstein (CRM-native signals, per the Agentforce description [1]), Claude (long call and email summarisation), Microsoft 365 Copilot (meeting and email work) and Gainsight AI (the dedicated CS platform, if licensed). Gamma and Gemini can be covered briefly.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well: Salesforce Einstein and Gainsight AI are the CS-native tools. Gamma is a weak fit, useful only for QBR decks. The list omits Salesforce Agentforce by name; the RSM article describes Agentforce as the renewal/health agent in Salesforce [1], so confirm whether 'Einstein' in the handbook is meant to cover it. Gainsight's Staircase AI is not on the list (not verified from an opened page).

departments.name: Customer Support & Contact Center
ai_use_cases: Autonomous first-line resolution: Intercom's Fin, powered by Claude, reports a 51% average out-of-the-box resolution rate, up to 86% for some customers, and response times cut from 30 minutes to seconds (vendor-reported) [1]
Multilingual support: Fin answers in over 45 languages with a configurable tone of voice and answer length per business [1]

Agent copilots: Zendesk reports 73% of agents believe an AI copilot would help them do their job better, and 90% of 'CX Trendsetters' report positive returns on AI tools for agents (vendor survey) [2]
Zendesk customer Vagaro reports AI resolved 44% of incoming requests, cut resolution time by 87% and reached 92% CSAT (customer quote in vendor report) [2]
Knowledge search: Intercom's VP of AI says support reps spend a lot of time searching for authoritative answers to questions they have seen before, which AI retrieval addresses [1]
Ticket classification and routing: handbook use case; no opened source with measured results, so no outcome is claimed here (not verified)
departments.capstone_deliverable: A 'support assistant pack' on a synthetic or anonymised set of 30 tickets. It contains a classification scheme with AI labels checked against human labels (accuracy and error log), 10 agent-assist draft replies edited by the learner with change notes, and 3 knowledge-base article drafts. Include the documented prompts, an escalation rule list (when AI must hand off to a human) and measured handling-time saving. Sized for Core-tier hours of about 8-10.
departments.data_risks: Customer PII, order and account details, payment references (PCI DSS if card data appears), sometimes health or other special-category data, and call recordings. GDPR applies to transcripts, retention and any automated decisions. Rules: mask card numbers and IDs before AI use; use only the helpdesk's governed AI, not public chatbots; disclose AI to customers and offer a human route; do not let AI promise refunds or policy exceptions. Zendesk links shadow AI use to privacy, security and service-quality risk [2]. Regulator guidance specific to contact-centre recordings was not checked, so that point is not verified.
departments.adoption_kpis: AI resolution (containment) rate with CSAT on AI-resolved tickets; average handle time and first response time; percentage of agent drafts accepted with minor edits; knowledge-article usage and gap-closure rate; escalation-to-human rate and reopen rate.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Put most Core hours into using the helpdesk's AI (agent assist, reply drafting, KB search) with strict redaction and escalation rules. Prioritise Zendesk AI or Intercom Fin (whichever the company runs), ServiceNow Now Assist (if it is the ticketing platform), and Claude for tone editing and KB drafting. Gemini is a general fallback.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit overall. Zendesk AI and Intercom Fin are competing platforms, so most teams will use only one and training should follow the deployed platform. Gemini and Claude are general assistants and should be limited to redacted content. Any handbook omission of Salesforce service tooling or Zendesk's Forethought acquisition is not verified. The Intercom page shows Fin is built on Claude [1].

departments.name: Customer Experience & Service Design
ai_use_cases: Omnichannel feedback analysis: Qualtrics (March 2025 release) combines structured and unstructured feedback across channels to give a complete view of the customer experience (vendor press release) [1]

Adaptive surveys: Qualtrics Conversational Feedback adapts questions in real time and prompts follow-ups on vague answers; the vendor says more than 50 brands use it, doubling feedback collected, with 90% of respondents answering follow-ups [1]
Behavioural friction detection: digital experience analytics use rage-clicks and mouse thrashing, heatmaps and funnels to find where customers abandon [1]
Frontline insight: Location Experience Hub shows store managers trending scores and AI-personalised responses [1]
Benchmarking and competitor insight on demand through Qualtrics Edge Instant Insights [1]
Human-centric AI service design: Zendesk reports 64% of consumers are more likely to trust AI agents with friendly, empathetic traits, a design input for service journeys (vendor survey) [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A voice-of-customer insight brief built from a provided set of 200 anonymised survey comments and tickets. Deliver AI-generated themes, human-verified theme counts with quote evidence, a current-state journey map with 3 pain points, and 2 service-design recommendations with an impact hypothesis. Include documented prompts, a validation log of AI-versus-human coding disagreements and time saved. Sized for about 12-16 Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Free-text feedback often contains names, contact details, complaints about individuals and sometimes health or financial detail; survey and call data fall under GDPR/UK GDPR (purpose limitation, consent for follow-up, retention). Rules: anonymise verbatims before using general assistants; keep raw data inside the survey platform's governed AI; never present AI theme percentages without checking against the source data; do not treat synthetic respondents as real customers.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time from data close to insight readout; percentage of themes validated by human coding sample; number of verbatims analysed per study; share of insights that lead to a logged service change; survey response and follow-up completion rates.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Focus on VoC synthesis with verification, journey-mapping workflows, and insight storytelling. Prioritise Qualtrics AI (where the survey data lives), Claude (long-context coding of verbatims), Microsoft 365 Copilot (reports, decks) and ChatGPT Enterprise only if it is the approved analysis tool. Canva Magic Studio is for visuals only.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Qualtrics AI is a strong fit. Canva Magic Studio is a weak fit for analysis and suits only journey-map visuals or stakeholder one-pagers. Whether the handbook omits dedicated research-repository tools such as Dovetail, or a journey-mapping tool, is not verified from an opened page. Qualtrics' own page is a vendor press release, so outcome claims need local testing [1].

departments.name: Product Management
ai_use_cases: Backlog decomposition: Jira's Rovo Work Breakdown suggests child work items from a parent item, which the user can accept, edit or decline before Jira creates them [2]

Story and acceptance-criteria drafting: a practitioner article reports Atlassian documentation shows Rovo generating user stories, subtasks, acceptance criteria and QA edge cases in the work-item editor [2]

Adoption signal: IdeaPlan's 2026 report (as cited) says 41% of product professionals use AI to generate user stories and 73% use AI tools weekly or daily; the article warns this is a synthesized signal, not an audited census [2]
Evidence-to-spec tools: Productboard Spark synthesises customer evidence, ranks opportunities and drafts delivery-oriented specifications [2]
Planning calculations: Rovo writes Jira formula fields from plain-language descriptions, for example weighted priority scores [1]
Space setup: Rovo can generate a Jira space with workflows, work types, views and suggested first work items from a natural-language description or attached context such as Confluence pages [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A one-page PRD plus a refined backlog slice for a real or sample feature. The AI-drafted PRD must be annotated with the PM's corrections, with each assumption linked to a source (customer quotes, usage data). Include 8 user stories with acceptance criteria, a release-note draft, the prompt log and a time-saved comparison. Sized for about 8-10 Core-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unreleased roadmap and pricing (commercially confidential, possible MNPI for listed companies), customer feedback with personal data (GDPR), partner NDA material and source code excerpts. Rules: only approved tools with enterprise data protection; do not paste roadmap or customer verbatims into consumer tools; anonymise feedback; the PM remains accountable for every requirement, since AI reduces blank-page work but does not remove accountability for the backlog [2].
departments.adoption_kpis: Time from idea to refinement-ready epic; percentage of stories accepted with minor edits; backlog items with complete acceptance criteria; PRD review cycles per feature; weekly active AI users among PMs.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Core-tier time should go to PRD drafting and critique, story and acceptance-criteria generation, and release communication, with verification habits. Prioritise Jira Atlassian Intelligence/Rovo (where the backlog lives), Claude (long PRD and research reasoning), NotebookLM (grounded synthesis over research docs) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (meetings, docs).
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well. Gamma is a weak fit beyond roadmap and stakeholder decks. The practitioner article names product-management platforms that may be absent from the list: Productboard Spark, Aha! Elle and Linear's agent [2]. The article is a training-vendor blog, so treat its tool comparisons as indicative. The article is titled around 'Atlassian Intelligence' while the Atlassian release post only names Rovo, so the handbook name may need updating [1][2].

Refonte Learning: Inside Jira's AI Backlog Tools (Aug 2026)

departments.name: Product Design & UX Research
ai_use_cases: Research synthesis on the canvas: Figma's AI agent summarises user feedback and interview notes, organises feedback themes and links findings to the relevant frames (vendor page) [1]
Design audits: the same agent audits screens for usability and accessibility issues [1]
Generation from the design system: Figma's agent generates and refines designs using actual components, tokens and variables, with parallel prompting and shareable threads [1]

Professional adoption: an NN/g survey of 841 UX professionals (July-August 2023) found 92% had used a generative AI tool (NN/g notes possible selection bias), and the most common activity was text-content generation and editing [2]
Four roles for generative AI in UX work: content editor, research assistant, ideation partner and design assistant [2]
Summarising qualitative sessions: NN/g tested AI 'insight generators' that summarise research sessions from transcripts alone, and found they miss context [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A usability-findings pack from 5 anonymised session transcripts or notes. Deliver AI-generated themes, the researcher's validated theme list with evidence quotes and an explicit list of what AI missed or invented, a wireframe concept with UX copy variants, and documented prompts. Include time saved and a note on which findings need real-user confirmation. Sized for about 12-16 Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Participant recordings, transcripts and demographics (GDPR/UK GDPR, consent scope and retention limits), unreleased designs and IP, and sometimes health-related data from usability sessions. Rules: check the consent form permits AI processing; anonymise before upload; keep unreleased designs inside approved tools. NN/g warns that AI insight generators do not accept product or user background and can give vague recommendations [3]; this article is from 2023 and NN/g itself notes many tools have improved since.
departments.adoption_kpis: Synthesis time per study; share of AI-generated themes confirmed by the researcher; number of design iterations explored per sprint; usability issues found per audit; accessibility defects caught before handoff.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Advanced hours should go to research synthesis with verification, wireframe and UX-copy ideation, and critique of AI output. Prioritise Figma AI (design and audit in the canvas), FigJam AI (affinity clustering and workshops, per the handbook), Claude (transcript analysis, UX writing) and ChatGPT Enterprise or Gemini only as a second opinion.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Figma AI and FigJam AI fit well. Canva Magic Studio is a weak fit for product UX, better for marketing assets. Whether the handbook omits dedicated research-repository tools is not verified; Dovetail's summarisation feature is mentioned in the NN/g survey design [2] but its current capabilities were not verified. The most important caution is NN/g's: be skeptical of marketing claims from AI research tools [3].

UX Research: added NN/g's own selection-bias caveat to the 92% statistic and noted NN/g says many tools have improved since 2023.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All six departments use AI in the same way. An assistant drafts code, tests, infrastructure templates, runbooks or knowledge articles. A human then verifies the draft against something that can pass or fail: a test run, a plan or dry-run, or telemetry. Claude Code's own best-practice guidance says to give the agent a check it can run. Shared risks are source code and credentials pasted into prompts, hallucinated or insecure output, and agents acting with broad permissions on production systems or ERP. Departments 41-44 should train together on agentic coding, verification gates and secrets hygiene, and 43-45 together on cloud and ticket-system tooling. Department 46 should join 45 for ticket and knowledge workflows, and 46 should train with Finance on SAP data. Evidence quality is uneven. Most quantified claims come from vendors or from a single company's self-report, so managers should measure their own baselines. ServiceNow, Salesforce, Dynatrace and Cursor claims could not be verified because those pages could not be opened.

departments.name: Software Engineering - Applications
ai_use_cases: Inline code completion and chat in the IDE with GitHub Copilot. A Zoominfo rollout to more than 400 developers measured acceptance rates (33% of suggestions, 20% of lines of code) and satisfaction. [1]
Developers self-reported a median 20% reduction in task time, with 77% saying work quality improved. These are survey results, not measured output. [1]

A randomized controlled trial at Accenture used DevOps telemetry plus a survey and found high adoption and satisfaction. The 'up to 55% faster' figure comes from GitHub's earlier lab studies, which the same post cites, not from the Accenture trial. This is vendor-run research. [2]
Generating unit tests, debugging and documenting code in the IDE with Gemini Code Assist, which cites sources when it quotes at length. [3]
Agentic coding in the terminal or IDE with Claude Code, using checkpoints to rewind changes. Subagents and hooks are described as Agent SDK support for custom workflows. [4]
Code review support: Zoominfo flagged limits in domain-specific context and the need to vet generated code. [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Refactor or document one real module (non-production data) using an approved assistant. Deliver the merged pull request, a prompt log, the tests that gate it, a security review of the AI-generated diff, and a measured before-and-after time comparison against a similar manual task. Assessed against a rubric on correctness, test evidence and honest reporting of rework.
departments.data_risks: Source code, credentials and API keys, proprietary algorithms and customer data in test fixtures. Rules: no secrets or production data in prompts; use enterprise-licensed tools with data-retention terms checked; review licence and citation flags on suggestions; treat generated code as untrusted until tested and scanned. Regulatory hooks (GDPR for personal data in fixtures) apply but were not covered by sources.
departments.adoption_kpis: Weekly active users as a share of licences; suggestion acceptance rate; pull request cycle time against a pre-rollout baseline; developer satisfaction survey score; defect or revert rate on AI-assisted changes.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Core tier, so most hours go to hands-on practice, then a short module on risk. Prioritise GitHub Copilot (the most evidence of enterprise rollout), Claude Code (agentic multi-file work with verification) and Gemini Code Assist (a Google Cloud shop). Spend a block on verification habits: run tests, review diffs, never accept blindly.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit overall. Gemini Code Assist's own documentation says new Standard and Enterprise subscriptions are no longer available for purchase, so confirm availability before teaching it. [3] Cursor is listed but no opened page covers it: not verified. ChatGPT Enterprise is a general assistant and is a weaker fit for IDE work than the others (not verified).

departments.name: Quality Engineering & Testing
ai_use_cases: Test case design and requirements refinement with an LLM assistant; the World Quality Report 2025 says these now lead GenAI adoption in quality engineering [1].
Generating first-draft Playwright or Selenium specs from a prompt, user story or recording; reviewers must make each test fail before trusting it [2].
Self-healing locators that repair selectors when markup changes; each heal should be reviewed, as it can hide a regression [2].
Failure triage that turns a wall of failed tests into a probable cause [2].
Test selection and flake detection to decide what to run and what to trust; keep a scheduled full run as a backstop [2].
Defect analysis and reporting, the earlier GenAI use now being overtaken by input-side work such as test design [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: Within about 12 hours: take one real user story, produce an AI-drafted Playwright suite of at least 10 tests, and show that each test fails against a deliberately broken build before it passes. Submit the prompt log, a review checklist covering hallucinated selectors and assertions, a heal-review record, and measured time versus manual authoring.
departments.data_risks: Test environments often hold copies of production data, including personal data (GDPR), payment card data (PCI DSS) and health data (HIPAA). Rules: use synthetic or masked data in prompts, never paste credentials or proprietary source into unsanctioned tools, and keep a human reviewer for all generated tests. The WQR 2025 ranks data privacy (67%) and hallucination or reliability (60%) among the top barriers [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: 1) Share of new tests drafted with AI and merged after review. 2) Test authoring time versus baseline (WQR reports an average 19% productivity gain, with one third seeing minimal gains [1]). 3) Flaky-test rate and failures triaged per engineer. 4) Escaped-defect rate for AI-assisted versus manual suites. 5) Healed locators reviewed within one sprint (%).
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Most hours on prompting for test design and on validating AI output (mutation and fail-first checks), because generated tests can be confidently wrong [2]. Prioritise Playwright (the execution target), GitHub Copilot or Claude Code (drafting and refactoring specs) and ChatGPT Enterprise (requirements refinement). Spend little time on self-healing until locator hygiene is covered; the source notes stable test ids fix the same brittleness permanently [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well: Playwright is a framework rather than an AI tool, but it is the natural target for generated tests. Gemini Code Assist is a generic coding assistant with no testing-specific evidence found. Omitted: AI-native testing platforms such as OpenText, Tricentis and mabl. The WQR press release notes OpenText was recognised as a Leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI-Augmented Software Testing Tools [1]; Tricentis and mabl were not verified from an opened page. Note the WQR is co-published by OpenText, a vendor in this space.

departments.name: Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Engineering
ai_use_cases: Cost optimisation in the AWS console: Amazon Q Developer gives rightsizing, Savings Plan and Reserved Instance, and idle-resource recommendations and explains how each was calculated. [1]
Multi-step troubleshooting and mapping of relationships across AWS resources through natural-language chat. [1]
Generating and refining Terraform, kubectl manifests and gcloud commands in Gemini Cloud Assist, with IAM policy help and simulation in chat. [2]
Designing, operating, optimising and troubleshooting Azure apps in Azure Copilot, which acts within the user's permissions and requires confirmation for actions. [3]

Agentic infrastructure-as-code authoring with Claude Code. Its best-practice guide advises giving the agent a pass/fail check and using plan mode; running terraform plan as that check is this handbook's suggestion, not stated by the source. [4]
departments.capstone_deliverable: For a sandbox account, produce a Terraform module using an AI assistant, run plan and a policy scan, and deliver a cost-reduction analysis built from assistant recommendations that you independently verify against billing data. Include the prompt log, a list of assistant errors found, and time saved.
departments.data_risks: Cloud credentials, account IDs, network topology, IAM policies, and logs that can contain customer data (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS). Rules: least-privilege access for any assistant, since the assistants act with the user's permissions [3]; human approval before apply; no secrets in prompts; verify recommendations against billing before acting.
departments.adoption_kpis: Cost savings realised from AI recommendations, verified; time to draft a reviewed IaC change; proportion of AI-generated IaC passing policy checks first time; troubleshooting time for common incidents; number of assistant-caused misconfigurations.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Specialist tier: depth on tools matching your cloud provider. Prioritise the assistant native to your cloud (Amazon Q Developer, Azure Copilot or Gemini Code Assist), plus Claude Code for cross-cloud IaC, plus GitHub Copilot for pipeline files (not verified). Spend hours on plan review and permission scoping.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list mixes three clouds; teach each team only its own. Amazon Q Developer's page says AWS will end support for its IDE plugins on 30 April 2027 and points to Kiro as the alternative, and Gemini Code Assist is no longer sold as a new subscription, so both need availability checks. [5][6] Gemini Cloud Assist is the relevant Google product and is not named in the handbook. [2]

departments.name: DevOps & Site Reliability Engineering
ai_use_cases: Autonomous alert investigation: Datadog Bits AI SRE analyses runbooks and telemetry, forms hypothetical root causes, validates its findings and delivers a conclusion to collaboration tools before on-call staff log in (vendor claim: hours to minutes). [1]

At Nulab, a small SRE team uses Bits Investigation across logs, metrics and traces; many low-priority alerts that took at least 30 minutes can now be triaged in under 5 minutes. This is a vendor-published case study. [2]
Natural-language investigation across infrastructure and costs, replacing hand-written queries. [2]
Verification loops in Claude Code: running a check the agent can read, such as a test or build. Applying this to runbook and pipeline scripts is this handbook's extrapolation. [3]
Runbook drafting by a general assistant (not verified in the sources); Bits posts its conclusion in collaboration tools. [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Using a past incident (sanitised), have an AI assistant draft a runbook and an investigation timeline. Compare its root-cause hypothesis with the actual post-mortem, and deliver the runbook, the prompt log, an accuracy assessment (hits, misses, unsupported claims) and time saved.
departments.data_risks: Logs and traces can contain personal data (GDPR), health data (HIPAA) and credentials; incident records may contain security-sensitive detail. Rules: redact before sharing outside the observability platform; use role-based access (Datadog advertises RBAC and HIPAA-regulated workload support for Bits AI SRE [1]); AI conclusions are hypotheses requiring human confirmation before changes to production.
departments.adoption_kpis: Mean time to acknowledge and to resolve; share of alerts with an AI investigation accepted as correct; false-hypothesis rate; runbook coverage of top alert types; on-call hours saved.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Specialist tier: hours on incident-style simulations. Prioritise the observability-native agent (Datadog Bits AI) and Claude Code for runbooks and scripts, plus GitHub Copilot for pipeline files (not verified). Train on confirming AI root causes rather than trusting them.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Datadog and Dynatrace are each relevant only if the company uses them; teach the one in use. Dynatrace Davis AI could not be verified from an opened page. Gemini Code Assist as a weaker fit for incident work is the author's judgement (not verified); check its new-subscription availability. Evidence is mostly vendor-published.

departments.name: IT Infrastructure & End-User Computing
ai_use_cases: Ticket deflection through AI self-service; ServiceNow's internal deployments reportedly reached deflection of up to about 54% on common issue-reporting forms, vendor-reported and cited second-hand [1].
Resolved tickets turned into draft knowledge articles, with the AI identifying which existing article to update and a human reviewing before publication [1].
Semantic search or RAG over the knowledge base so users can describe a problem in plain language [1].
Agentic resolution of requests across several tools; the article warns that much vendor 'agentic AI' is still advisory GenAI [1].
Estimating the blast radius of a planned change from a clean CMDB and composite AI before release [1].
Drafting change communications and impact summaries for stakeholders using GenAI, grounded by causal AI against CMDB topology [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: Within about 8 hours: audit the 20 most-requested end-user issues, then deliver five AI-drafted knowledge articles reviewed by a senior technician. Include the prompt log, a staleness check on existing articles, and a deflection report using the 'full AI resolution, no recontact within 72 hours' definition, plus estimated time saved per ticket.
departments.data_risks: Tickets and endpoint logs contain employee personal data (GDPR, employment law), credentials, device and network details, and sometimes regulated data. Rules: redact identifiers before prompting, use only enterprise-approved tools, and require human approval for irreversible autonomous actions. The source names data leakage, prompt injection and irreversible autonomous actions as the consistent production risks [1], and warns that a knowledge-base-grounded agent can expose documents users should not see [1]. Gartner found 69% of organizations suspect or confirm prohibited public GenAI use (survey of 302 cybersecurity leaders) [2].
departments.adoption_kpis: 1) True AI resolution rate (no recontact in 72 hours), not dashboard deflection; the source says true rates often run 15-25% below vendor dashboards [1]. 2) Mean time to resolve for AI-assisted tickets. 3) Knowledge articles created from tickets and share reviewed within SLA. 4) Stale article share in the knowledge base. 5) Employee CSAT after AI-handled contacts.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on knowledge-base hygiene and grounding, since the source calls it the largest predictor of AI ITSM ROI [1], then on safe use of agents with approval gates. Prioritise ServiceNow Now Assist (ticket workflow), Microsoft 365 Copilot (documentation and communications), and Claude or Gemini (article drafting and troubleshooting analysis); these tool names are not covered by the cited sources. Add a short module on shadow AI policy [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: ServiceNow Now Assist fits the service-desk workflow (the source mentions ServiceNow only for the deflection figure, not Now Assist features). Microsoft Security Copilot is a weaker fit for routine end-user support, because it targets security operations (this is my judgement, not stated in an opened source). The list names no end-user device-management or non-ServiceNow ITSM AI tooling; I did not verify specific omitted products. Caveat: the main source is written by the CEO of a competing AI-native ITSM vendor (Ravenna), so its framing of vendors is not neutral.

departments.name: Enterprise Applications & ERP
ai_use_cases: Conversational assistance inside SAP S/4HANA, SuccessFactors, Ariba and Customer Experience; the article says finance users can request margin forecasts and supply chain managers can simulate disruptions [1].
Procurement: summarising supplier risk, generating RFQs and initiating approvals in Ariba through Joule [1].
Customer-dispute handling; a European auto parts supplier reportedly cut time-to-resolve in S/4HANA by 40% (vendor-sourced, unaudited, unnamed customer) [1].
HR service automation; a global consumer goods company reportedly automates 60% of HR service requests with Joule (vendor-sourced, unnamed customer) [1].
ERP migration and implementation support; Joule was trained on SAP consulting assets to assist ERP implementations (2024 announcement) [2].
Cross-assistant integration, with Joule to be integrated with Microsoft Copilot for 365 and Google Cloud's Gemini (2024 announcement) [2].
departments.capstone_deliverable: Within about 16 hours: for one ERP or CRM process (for example supplier dispute handling), deliver a documented AI-assisted workflow with a role-and-permission map, ten validated test prompts checked against system-of-record data, an exception log of wrong or unauthorised answers, and a before-and-after time measurement.
departments.data_risks: ERP and CRM systems hold financial records (SOX), personal data of customers and employees (GDPR, employment law), supplier pricing and possibly material non-public information. Rules: AI must respect existing role-based permissions, outputs must be checked against the system of record before posting, and no records go into unsanctioned tools. ERP Today states Joule agent activity is governed and auditable via SAP LeanIX (a vendor-friendly claim) [1]. Gartner flags shadow AI, vendor lock-in and data sovereignty as blind spots [3].
departments.adoption_kpis: 1) Share of target tasks completed through the embedded assistant. 2) Time-to-resolve for disputes or support requests versus baseline. 3) Error rate: AI answers corrected on validation. 4) Access or permission violations detected in AI interactions. 5) Active users per licence (%).
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Focus on embedded, permission-aware assistants and on validating outputs against the system of record, because a wrong ERP action has financial consequences. Prioritise SAP Joule (embedded in S/4HANA, Ariba) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (documentation, with Joule integration noted [2]); Salesforce Einstein (CRM) is not verified from an opened source. Use Claude or Gemini mainly for functional specs and test scripts.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: SAP Joule fits, but only helps teams running SAP, so training should be tailored to the company's actual stack. Salesforce Einstein's fit is not verified from an opened source. The list omits Oracle, Workday AI (listed for HR departments but not here), and Dynamics-type suites; I did not verify any omitted tool for this function. Customer outcomes found are vendor-sourced, so confidence is limited.

deptClusters.verification_notes: All cited URLs opened, and most specific claims matched their sources (Zoominfo figures, Accenture RCT design, Meta 73%, AWS, Google, Azure, Datadog, Security Copilot, SAP). Errors found were misattributions and extrapolations rather than fabrications. Remaining weaknesses are heavy reliance on vendor pages and a single source for department 46, so the low confidence there and in 42 and 45 stands. Cursor, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Dynatrace and GitHub Copilot for pipeline files were not checked against any opened page. Re-research of departments 42, 45, 46 (second pass): All seven cited pages opened and supported the main statistics (WQR 19%, 67%, 60%, test-design lead; Gartner 69%; Joule 60% and 40% figures; the ITSM 72-hour definition and the 54% ServiceNow figure). The corrections were the removal of one unsupported claim, a few tightened wordings, and not-verified labels on tool names the sources do not cover. Evidence is mostly vendor-adjacent or opinion pieces (OpenText co-publishes the WQR, the ITSM author runs a competitor, ERP Today is promotional), so confidence stays medium, medium and low.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All five departments sit on sensitive data and on the platforms that hold it, so the strongest pattern is vendor-embedded AI that inherits existing access controls (Security Copilot, Purview, Snowflake RBAC, Power BI semantic models) and works best on well-prepared metadata. Shared risks are over-sharing through broad permissions, unverified AI output feeding decisions (alert verdicts, generated SQL, dashboard answers), and agents taking actions, so human approval gates and evaluation datasets are common requirements. Departments 47 and 48 should train together on SOC and governance handoffs and AI-agent oversight, and 49, 50 and 51 on semantic-layer preparation, answer validation and evaluation-driven development. All five should share one module on governing AI (NIST AI RMF and its generative AI profile) and on data classification. Research limit: most claims are vendor-reported, and regulatory hooks beyond NIST are general knowledge, not verified.

departments.name: Cybersecurity Operations
ai_use_cases: Phishing triage agent in Defender autonomously handles and closes false-positive alerts; Microsoft reports SOC analysts found malicious emails up to 550% faster, and one customer quote cites nearly 200 hours saved monthly (vendor-reported) [1]
Incident investigation: summarise complex alerts into actionable summaries with step-by-step response guidance [1]
Natural-language to query-script conversion and script reverse-engineering so team members can run technical tasks (page says query-language scripts; KQL specifically not verified) [1]
Stakeholder incident reporting, tailored to the audience [1]

Agentic detection triage with parallel cross-domain investigation agents; CrowdStrike lists over 98% decision accuracy (benchmarked against its Falcon Complete MDR decisions) and 70% reduced manual effort in investigations (vendor figures) [2]
No-code custom security agents; actions can run autonomously or require human approval before running [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Triage a set of 20 anonymised or synthetic alerts with an AI assistant, producing one incident summary plus a hunting query for analyst review. Include documented prompts, a verdict-versus-analyst comparison table with errors flagged, and minutes saved per alert. Sources: vendor docs and the team's own runbook. Sized for a Specialist-tier time budget.
departments.data_risks: Handles logs with personal data, credentials, indicators tied to employees and customers, and incident details that may be privileged or subject to breach notification (GDPR and similar; not verified in opened sources). Rules: use only tenant-approved tools; never paste raw incident data into consumer tools; keep humans approving containment actions; log prompts and outputs as evidence. Charlotte AI is described as ISO 42001-certified with answers traceable to source data [2].
departments.adoption_kpis: Mean time to triage and respond; share of alerts auto-closed and later confirmed correct; analyst override rate; hours saved per month; percentage of hunting queries AI-drafted and accepted.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on hands-on triage and validation with Microsoft Security Copilot and CrowdStrike Charlotte AI (whichever the SOC runs), because the vendors position them for alert triage and investigation. Add Claude for query drafting and report writing on sanitised data. Teach override and approval-gate practice and error spotting rather than prompting basics.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well on the tool-specific side. Gemini and Claude are general assistants and are secondary for a SOC unless wired to approved data. Google Gemini in Security was not verified in an opened source. Both opened pages show the platform agents are bound to their own ecosystem (Defender/Sentinel or Falcon), so staff should learn the one they own. departments.name: Security Governance, Risk & Privacy
ai_use_cases: Discover and monitor generative AI use via Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI as the front door to discover, secure and apply compliance controls for AI usage (one-click policies not verified) [1]
Use sensitivity labels so AI apps only return data a user may access [1]
Assess AI apps in use across Microsoft Copilots (incl. Security Copilot, Copilot in Fabric), Entra-registered apps, ChatGPT Enterprise and Claude Enterprise, and other AI apps [1]
Structure AI risk assessments around the NIST AI RMF and its Generative AI Profile (NIST-AI-600-1, July 2024) [2]
Security Copilot agents span Defender, Entra, Intune and Purview to help detect, investigate and respond (specific Purview data-security-investigation scenario not verified) [3]

departments.capstone_deliverable: A one-page AI risk assessment for one approved AI tool, mapped to NIST AI RMF functions and the Generative AI Profile, listing data categories, label and permission checks, residual risks and owner. departments.tool_fit_commentary: Purview fits strongly and is documented as covering many AI apps [1]. ServiceNow Now Assist was not verified in an opened source. departments.name: Data Engineering & Data Platforms
ai_use_cases: Genie Code plans multistep tasks as a structured plan the user reviews and approves before it executes; used for pipelines, notebook and SQL analysis (Databricks) [1]
Exploratory data analysis in notebooks and SQL [1]
Text-to-SQL for business questions through Snowflake Cortex Analyst over a semantic model, executed under Snowflake RBAC [2]
Semantic model definitions with access modifiers and verified queries to improve SQL accuracy [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Deliver one pipeline or semantic view built with AI help: code, tests, data-quality checks and a lineage note. Include documented prompts, a log of AI mistakes caught in review, and measured build-time saved versus the team baseline.
departments.data_risks: Platforms hold personal, financial and health data (GDPR, SOX, HIPAA, PCI DSS depending on sector; not verified in sources). Rules: Cortex Analyst does not train on customer data and respects RBAC, with default Snowflake-hosted models keeping data inside Snowflake's governance boundary [2]; still restrict who gets the AI role, since CORTEX_USER is granted to PUBLIC by default (CORTEX_ANALYST_USER is the narrower role) [2]. Never paste production rows into unapproved tools; review generated SQL before running on production.
departments.adoption_kpis: Pipeline build and fix cycle time; share of AI-generated SQL accepted without edit; data-quality incidents per release; percentage of tables with semantic metadata; users with the AI role against the approved list.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Databricks Assistant/Genie Code and Snowflake Cortex AI (platform-native, governed), plus Claude Code and GitHub Copilot for pipeline code and tests. Hours go to review discipline, semantic metadata and access control rather than prompt tricks.

departments.name: Business Intelligence & Analytics
ai_use_cases: Business users chat with their data in Power BI through a standalone Copilot, a report pane or app-scoped Copilot [1]
Report summaries and ad hoc analysis that an analyst would otherwise be asked for [1]
DAX measure generation and model changes proposed and applied by Copilot in the Power BI service web modeling experience [2]
Verified answers prepared by app authors for common questions, to raise consistency [1]
Defining focused test questions with expected measure, grouping, date basis, filters and validated results before rollout [2]
Natural-language questions over a governed semantic model with Snowflake Cortex Analyst as a comparison pattern [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: Prepare one semantic model for AI, write 10 test questions with validated answers, run them through Copilot, and report accuracy, failures and fixes. Include prompts, a dashboard narrative and time saved per report.
departments.data_risks: Dashboards expose financial, HR and customer data. Rules: app-scoped Copilot responses are limited to the app's content and the user's permissions, and unprepared models can give inaccurate results [1][2]; if the tenant or capacity is outside the US/EU data boundary Copilot is disabled by default unless the Fabric admin enables processing outside the region [1]. Do not paste exports into unapproved tools; verify numbers before they enter board or SOX-relevant reports (SOX: not verified in sources).
departments.adoption_kpis: Share of dashboards with AI narratives validated; Copilot answer accuracy on the test set; report requests handled self-serve; analyst hours saved; active Copilot users per month.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: As a Core tier, put most hours on Power BI Copilot (prepare model, ask, verify) and Claude/Gemini for narrative drafting from approved extracts. Tableau Pulse only if the company uses Tableau. Gamma gets minimal time.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Power BI Copilot fits; Copilot in Fabric is not supported on trial SKUs, only paid SKUs [1]. Tableau Pulse could not be verified: its vendor page failed to open (403). Gamma and ChatGPT Enterprise are marginal for analysis. Not verified: Databricks Genie and Snowflake Cortex Analyst as BI options, though Cortex Analyst is a documented platform [3].

departments.name: Research, Innovation & Emerging Technology
ai_use_cases: Startup and technology scouting: companies must look at thousands of startups a year, at the right maturity (TRL 1-9), to funnel down to the few worth co-innovating with; Mind the Bridge has built an AI scouting engine for this and scouting platforms are being 'productized'. [1]
Generative AI helps corporates define their own innovation challenges (Mind the Bridge says it has included such capabilities). [1]

AI-assisted idea generation and early-stage investment screening: algorithms crunch data from databases such as Crunchbase, Pitchbook and DealRoom, plus web conversation data, to spot emerging market niches. [1]

Patent-landscape reading: WIPO's 2026 GenAI update reports published families rising from about 14,000 (2023) to over 37,000 (2025) and LLMs overtaking GANs. An innovation team can summarise such reports into a scan with an LLM, checking figures against the source. [2]

Competitive-signal tracking: the same report names Nvidia, State Grid, Inspur and Bosch as new entrants, signalling industrial and utility firms entering GenAI patenting. This is useful for scanning adjacent-industry entrants. [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A 6-8 page technology scan on one emerging technology of the learner's choice. It includes a shortlist of 5 vendors or startups scored by TRL, at least 8 cited and validated sources (patent or analyst data checked against the originals), a one-page prototype plan with success metrics, the documented prompts used, and a measured time-saved comparison against a manual baseline. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unpublished R&D ideas, invention disclosures and partner or NDA material. Patentability can be lost if inventions are disclosed publicly, so no invention details go into consumer AI tools (handbook guidance, not from the cited sources). Startup data under NDA must stay in enterprise tools. Scouting output may include personal data about founders (GDPR). Third-party data licences (Crunchbase, Pitchbook) may restrict AI use (not verified). Every figure needs source verification, because vendor-claimed scouting results are self-reported.
departments.adoption_kpis: Hours per technology scan versus baseline; number of candidate startups screened per quarter; share of scan claims traced to a primary source; share of scouted leads reaching pilot; percentage of team using approved enterprise AI tools weekly.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on source-grounded research and verification (Perplexity Enterprise, Claude or Gemini), then on structured synthesis into a scan and prototype plan. Add a short block on prototyping with GitHub Copilot and on experiment documentation. Treat Gamma as a presentation convenience only. Cover confidentiality and IP rules first.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list suits desk research and synthesis. Gamma is a weak fit for the substantive work. The Körber article names dedicated scouting platforms that the handbook omits, including Glassdollar, Tracxn, Pitchbook and Mind the Bridge [1]. Whether WIPO's patent analytics services are listed or relevant is not verified. Both sources were opened, but neither tests the listed tools.

departments.name: Enterprise Architecture & Integration
ai_use_cases: Retroactive ADR generation: Equal Experts turned one-line decision statements into full ADRs with a metaprompt in Gemini 2.5 and ChatGPT. Outcome: dozens of ADRs in a single morning. [1]
Inferring missing ADRs: pasting high-level designs, slide packs or code into an LLM to propose implicit decisions that should be recorded, building a backlog of one-line candidates. [1]

Quality-checking ADRs: a different LLM prompt acts as a judge to critique generated ADRs for logical flaws before human review. A coding agent was also tried to find contradictions across ADRs, with variable success. [1]

Option and trade-off analysis: an architect supplies the criteria and AI researches and formats alternatives against the Salesforce Well-Architected Framework, using prompt chaining. Example single-org versus multi-org ADRs were drafted with Gemini 2.5 and reviewed by the named decision-makers. [2]
Suggesting reviewers: the prompt flags when security, networking or data privacy roles should review a given ADR. [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A set of 3 ADRs for a real or realistic integration decision (for example, API gateway versus event bus), each with at least 3 options scored against stated criteria. Each is generated from a documented metaprompt, then fact-checked, with every reference link verified and an AI-usage disclosure line. Include a short log of errors found in the AI draft and the time saved against writing one ADR manually.
departments.data_risks: Confidential solution designs, data models and business requirements; Salesforce warns that putting these into public LLMs risks data leakage and IP exposure, so check terms of service, disable training on inputs and use approved enterprise tools [2]. Network and security architecture, vendor contract terms, need-to-know access and GDPR or data-residency review are handbook guidance, not stated in the sources. Hallucinated references and invented product features are a documented risk [1]; Salesforce also warns that LLMs can make things up [2].
departments.adoption_kpis: ADRs produced per quarter and share with a recorded AI-usage disclosure; hours per ADR versus baseline; defects (wrong facts or dead links) found in review per ADR; backlog of undocumented decisions closed; time from decision to approved ADR.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Claude and ChatGPT Enterprise for metaprompted ADR drafting and a second-model critique pass, GitHub Copilot for inferring decisions from code, and Microsoft 365 Copilot for finding source documents. Most hours go on the review discipline: fact-checking, reference checking and keeping human ownership of the decision.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: General LLMs fit ADR drafting, as both sources show. Gamma is a weak fit for architecture work. Architecture-specific tooling (SAP LeanIX, ServiceNow Now Assist for Enterprise Architecture, Ardoq) may be absent from the list, but their AI capabilities were not verified here.

sources.title: Equal Experts: Accelerating ADRs with Generative AI
Salesforce Architecture Blog: Architectural Decisions, a Human-Led, AI-Powered Approach
